achievements.wikiText:
A Quest for Understanding is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Astellarn in the Dragonkin Laboratory with at least two pulsars active.

This achievement can only be completed in normal mode.

Astellarn periodically summons a pulsar star, which explodes for arena-wide cannonball damage. It is recommended to complete this achievement in a solo run as this minimises the waiting period for a second pulsar and also reduces its damage significantly from roughly 2,200 to 900.

Pulsar stars do not last indefinitely, and will despawn sometime after another pulsar appears. Players should reduce Astellarn's health to 5,000 before finishing her off when two pulsar stars are in the arena.

This achievement can only be completed in a private instance.

## Strategy

Drag Araxxor into the pool and wait for him to soak up 95-100% of the acid, so that the droplets that fall as he climbs up the ramp will not push the pool above 10%. Upon the ramp breaking, Araxxor must still be holding at least 40% acid to complete the achievement.

achievements.name: Akh Away Quickly
achievements.description: Defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode without anyone taking damage from Gorilla Akh and without reflecting damage from Modest Crocodiles.
achievements.wikiSummary: Akh Away Quickly is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode without anyone taking damage from gatekeeper gorilla akh and without reflecting damage from modest crocodile demons.
achievements.wikiText:
Akh Away Quickly is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode without anyone taking damage from gatekeeper gorilla akh and without reflecting damage from modest crocodile demons.

## Requirements

This achievement requires that no player receives damage from a gatekeeper gorilla akh during phases 2 and 4, and no player received reflected damage from a modest crocodile demon during phases 2 and 7. Any enrage can be used for this achievement, so it is recommended that players complete it at 100% enrage, unless they are looking to complete the perfect achievement, which requires 2000% enrage.

This achievement is failed if any player is hit by one of the aforementioned attacks, even if the damage is blocked by Barricade. Failing one of these requirements will display the message You have failed: Akh Away Quickly: A Gatekeeper Gorilla attacked <Player>. or You have failed: Akh Away Quickly: A Modest Crocodile reflected some of <Player>'s damage..

## Strategy

### Gorillas

Gorillas can only attack with melee, and can be stunned and bound. Use of Entangle to prevent them from moving is recommended, as it allows 24 seconds in which to kill them before it must be reapplied. If done at lower enrages, a high-damage stun such as Asphyxiate may kill the gorilla before it has a chance to attack.

Note that the gorillas will not aggro a player until an attack or spell is used on them, so in phase 4 it is recommended to not entangle the gorillas until their shields have been removed, as removing the shield will not draw their aggro.

### Crocodiles

The crocodiles will reflect damage if they are hit with any ability that has an adrenaline cost (or spends necromancy stacks). Thus, they should be hit with the highest damage basic abilities that the players have. These are often damage-over-time or multi-hit abilities. Necromancy players can make use of Invoke Death, Command Skeleton Warrior, and Command Putrid Zombie as these can deal high damage without costing adrenaline.

Amascut will only summon crocodiles in phase 7 if she targets the Crondis statue. Depending on the team's damage and the fight's enrage, it may be possible to ignore these crocodiles, however if this is done they care must be taken with multi-target abilities that may be reflected, such as Death Skulls or Hurricane.

## Achievement Set

Completing this achievement at 2000% enrage is one of the requirements for the Amascut, the Devourer (perfect) grandmaster achievement.

## Strategy

A player with strong gear should not even need to use any crystal in the first place, especially with Necromancy, as there is no crystal for it. Simply ignore them when they spawn.

If players log out during a kill, they will not be eligible for the achievement.

achievements.name: All Together Now
achievements.description: Defeat all four images of Yakamaru within ten seconds of one another.
achievements.wikiSummary: All Together Now is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful fight against Yakamaru where all four pools are blocked within ten seconds of each other.
achievements.wikiText:
All Together Now is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful fight against Yakamaru where all four pools are blocked within ten seconds of each other.

## Strategies

There should be at least one player tanking each image of Yakamaru, with players handling shark and stun pools carrying the planks. It is recommended to have one or two players with wands using Entangle on jellyfish. Weaken all four mirages to at most 20,000 life points before killing them simultaneously. The ten-second timer begins after the first pool is sealed with planks or sand. The easiest method is to "prefill" sand and tendril pools by lowering corresponding image's life points and having three players each fill the pools three times (resulting in nine out of the required ten fills), and having the image return to the pool. This reduces the time used to fill pools for the final time.

DPS group should start the mirage phase by damaging images in the sand pool, then the shark pool, and finally the tentacle pool. Players at the stun pool should solo their pool. When everyone is ready, the stun pool should be stunned to signal the start of finishing the pools as attempting to stun delays DPS.

## Trivia

• The achievement's name is a reference to the 1969 Beatles song "All Together Now".

achievements.name: All Together, Now!
achievements.description: Defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 1000% or higher enrage while every player is hit by each 'Crushing Soul' attack.
achievements.wikiSummary: All Together, Now! is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 1,000% or higher enrage while every player is hit by each 'Crushing Soul' attack.
achievements.wikiText:
All Together, Now! is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 1,000% or higher enrage while every player is hit by each 'Crushing Soul' attack.

## Requirements

This achievement requires every time Amascut uses her 'Crushing Soul' attack, which is the one accompanied by the voice line "Bend the Knee", that every player present in the arena is hit by it. It also requires that the enrage of the fight is at least 1000%. This attack is used in phases 1 and 3.

This achievement is failed if any time the Crushing Soul attack is used, there is a player not hit by it. The message You have failed: All Together, Now!. is displayed if this happens. In the event that a phase is ended early by bringing Amascut to her health threshold for that phase, such that the Crushing Soul attack is not used in that phase, then this does not invalidate the achievement.

## Strategy

Crushing Soul hits all players in a 3x3 around the base tank when it hits, with the damage shared among the players hit. When the attack is about to occur, the players should all Dive onto the same spot, before separating again. This can be done by having the base dive into the DPS pile, or vice versa.

achievements.wikiText:
Amascut, the Devourer (perfect) is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 2000% enrage while completing the listed achievements.

These listed achievements are all part of the Combat subcategory Amascut and are all members-only.

Completing this achievement unlocks the title [Name], Tumeken's Light.

## Requirements

There are 7 achievements in this group.

There is no failure message specific to the Perfect achievement, however if players see any failure message for any one of its constituent achievements then they will know that Perfect has been failed. It is recommended to turn the setting for "Achievement failure, progress, and eligibility messaging" to "All" so that messages from previously-completed constituent achievements will not be hidden.

## General strategy

At 2000% enrage, players will be afflicted with the Lone Soul debuff, which prevents players from being affected by Intercept, Heal Other, and Heal Group. Most notably, this means that players cannot Intercept a teammate with Barricade or Immortality to avoid damage. As an overview of what specific actions players need to do in each phase:

• Phase 1
• Prevent the volatile scarabs from spawning, and kill any that do spawn
• Phase 2
• Entangle the gorillas so they cannot attack any player
• Kill the crocodiles without reflecting damage
• Avoid all telegraphed floor AoE attacks in the side rooms
• Avoid the soulfire waves on the main arena
• Phase 3
• Prevent the volatile scarabs from spawning, and kill any that do spawn
• Avoid taking any damage from the square sanctum shockwaves
• Phase 4
• Entangle the gorillas so they cannot attack any player
• Avoid all telegraphed floor AoE attacks in the side rooms
• Avoid the soulfire waves on the main arena
• Avoid killing explosive scarabs unnecessarily, and throw any accidentally killed scarabs at Amascut or out of the arena
• As the phase ends, throw all remaining explosive scarabs out of the arena
• Phase 5
• Charge all 4 fragments before reforming Tumeken
• Intercept all green projectiles
• Kill all lightstealer akh before they can reach the fragments or Tumeken
• Phase 6
• Click all tears before they explode, and before reforming Tumeken
• Phase 7
• Correctly provoke Amascut toward each statue she calls
• Avoid all telegraphed floor AoE attacks
• (If present) Kill or ignore the crocodiles without reflecting damage
• (If present) Kill and throw all scarabs at Amascut

## Strategy breakdown

### Menaphiting My Way Through This

All that must be done is to provoke Amascut towards the correct altar in Phase 7. Knowing Amascut's voicelines and which altar is in which specific corner is beneficial. Players can use movement abilities or defensives to avoid or mitigate Amascut's projectile once she is provoked.

The altars appear in the following corners:

• Altar of Apmeken - north-west corner
• Altar of Scabaras - north-east corner
• Altar of Crondis - south-east corner
• Altar of Het - south-west corner

### Akh Away Quickly

Players must avoid taking damage from Gatekeeper gorilla akhs and reflecting damage from modest crocodile demons. Gorilla akhs are initially unaggressive, so team members can focus on taking down the crocodiles using basic abilities during phase 2. Crackling, Aftershock, Death Mark, and Conjures are also able to damage the crocodiles.

Gorilla akhs attack with melee and are able to stun players. Entangle can bind them for 24 seconds, and they can also be frozen and stunned. Gorillas may also be kited, for players in melee distance can avoid their attacks by moving out of the way. If the player is able to dodge without taking damage, then the achievement will not fail despite the gorilla attempting to attack them.

### Step aside, Scarab

Players must avoid taking damage from volatile and explosive scarab akhs.

Volatile scarab akhs spawn in phases 1 and 3 of the fight. Player can dive or run on their location to prevent them from spawning, and, once spawn, can be made vulnerable through the use of stuns. There are two ways to deal with this mechanic:

### Method 1 (phases 1 & 3):

With enough DPS, scarabs can be entirely skipped. In phase 1, if Amascut reaches her life points cap before scarabs are able to explode, then they will all disappear. In phase 3, players must bring Amascut to her life points cap before she says Tear them apart .

### Method 2 (phases 1 & 3):

If the team is lacking in DPS, the scarabs must be cleared from the arena through running over the cracks and killing them. An important note is that the base tank cannot do this, meaning the other four team members should spread throughout the arena and take care of scarabs while the base deals with Amascut.

This also means that the base tank will have to take Amascut's Crushing Soul special attack, indicated by the voiceline Bend the knee . Immortality is the most common method to do this, though the base must pay special attention in phase 3 due to Immortality's revival locking the player into place. They must be willing to move quickly to avoid Amascut's shockwaves.

### Phase 4

Unlike volatile scarabs, explosive scarabs spawn in phase 4. These do not need to be stunned to be killed, though they instead flip onto their back once they take 5,000 damage, initiating a charge. Being hit by their explosion will fail the achievement. However, throwing these scarabs at other monsters or scenery will have them explode on impact; this includes Amascut, soul obelisks, the chains found in each prison, and any of her akhs.

Explosive scarabs can also be thrown outside the arena to the south; if they're thrown far enough, they will also deal no damage. Throwing them out the eastern and western sides of the arena will not protect you from damage.

If someone throwing scarabs inside of a gateway accidentally throws it behind the gateway to an unreachable area, then they should enter the gateway before the scarab explodes to prevent the achievement from failing.

Any remaining scarab will flip over onto its back when Amascut initiates phase 5. At 2,000% enrage, her life points cap is 3,000,000, so the team should get off Amascut when she is close to the cap in order to preemptively begin killing and throwing scarabs into the dunes south of the arena. The scarabs on the edges should be deal with great care, for they can spawn where soul obelisks spawn, making them unreachable, and soul obelisks can also block a player's line of sight when trying to throw them. In addition, players on the edges may accidentally begin charging the fragments.

By doing this, the number of scarabs at the beginning of phase 5 can be reduced if enough are taken care of at the end of phase 4. Once phase 5 begins, throw every scarab that has flipped over at Amascut, obelisks, or the dunes to the south. Once this is done, begin the charging process.

### Phase 7

Explosive scarabs appear only if Amascut's calls upon the power of Scabaras. Though the deal no damage when they explode, the achievement will still fail if they do, meaning that every scarab that flips over must be thrown at Amascut.

### What Do You Mean I Could Make Multiple Trips?

This achievement requires all four fragments to be charged at once during phase 5. This can be done with a simple strategy:

• One member charges the far west fragment to full.
• One member charges the far east fragment to full.
• The south charger and two green tanks charge the centre west fragment to half.
• Once the centre west fragment is charged to half, the three then move to the centre east and charge it to full.
• The south charger needs to make sure lightstealer salawa akhs are not escaping them.
• The two team members who charged the far fragment then charge the second half of the centre west one.
• The other south charger needs to also deal with lightstealers.
• Tumeken should be reformed the tick Amascut says Your light will be snuffed out, once and for all . By timing it perfect, the team can skip one of her jumps.

By doing this, both centre fragments should reach a full charge at about the same time period, minimalising the time spent charging the fragment.

### Protector of the Sun God

This achievement requires Tumeken to not be damaged during phase 5 from both Amascut and lightstealer salawa akhs. The member who is first called by Amascut should be ready to tank her onslaught, while the other four members deal with the lightstealer akhs spawning from the south.

### No More Tears

Players must absorb every engulfing shadow tear during phase 6. These will charge up a magic hit that will deal more damage the more tears are absorbed, though it can be mitigated with defensives.

The jumper should pay close attention to how fast they're jumping. Stalling on the last platform after killing the last akh to allow the team to absorb all of the tears can be helpful, for if there are tears when the jumper claims Tumeken's light, then the achievement will fail.

### Dedicated Denial of Standing (here)

For this achievement, no team member must be damaged by Amascut's soulfire waves, shockwaves, or hieroglyphs throughout phases 2, 3, 4, and 7.

### Phase 2

Shockwaves appear in the prison of Apmeken. If a player is using Ranged or Magic, then all three chains can be safespotted.

Soulfire waves appear in the prison of Crondis and in the main arena once one player has grabbed a fragment of Tumeken and exits the prison. The far left and right chains in Crondis' prison can be safespotted with Ranged, Magic, and Necromancy, but players must dodge the waves for the centre chain.

In the main arena, soulfire waves follow a predictable pattern in three varying sets, emerging from the southern end of the arena. One particular set occupies a large portion of the central arena, meaning runners should be patient as they pass. Whenever a player begins getting close to the altar they're delivering their fragment to, the soulfire waves will cease. Setting a prism of salvation one tile east/west of the red outlines that form the central square of the arena should be enough for the first runner to safely traverse the arena.

Players should be weary of lightstealer salawa akhs, who will pounce on one of the runner for heavy melee damage.

One method of doing this is to burst one prison of the arena, usually the west prison as it's safer. This will allow the runner to deliver the fragment as fast as possible, staggering Amascut. When Amascut is staggered, floor hazards in both the main arena and prisons will temporarily cease, allowing the other runner safety.

### Phase 3

Amascut will emit four sets of Devourer's Shockwaves with every special attack.

Players using magic or ranged should position themselves one tile behind the green cracks that appear in the northern pyramids. This will provide them enough distance to avoid the first three sets. The last set requires magers and rangers to walk forward one tile.

Players using necromancy or melee must avoid the second and third sets. Necromancers should stand three tiles back from Amascut, walk back a tile for the second set, then walk back in a tile for the third set. Players using melee can walk under Amascut for the second set.

If the base tank is tanking the Crushing Soul attack, then they will temporarily be bound when revived by Immortality. Due to this, the base must use ranged or magic in order to not get hit by shockwaves; they have roughly two ticks to move to a safe location after being revived by Immortality, so great caution must be advised, especially if Amascut is about to use her rapid swipes against the base.

If clearing scarabs due to lower DPS, players should wait until the last ring of shockwaves before diving back towards Amascut.

### Phase 4

Phase 4 operates similarly to phase 2.

Soulfire waves appear in the prison of Scabaras. Like with Crondis, the far east and west chains can be safespotted.

Shockwaves appear in the prison of Het. One particular ring of shockwaves in Het's prison is extremely large and must be avoided for the southern two chains. However, players using magic and ranged can safespot the south two chains and avoid the large shockwave. The eastern chain can be fully safepsotted.

Unlike phase 2, due to the closer proximity of the altars, soulfire waves will not stop spawning when the runner gets close, so great caution is advised for runners. The moment the fragment is deposited, runners are able to use movement abilities again.

### Phase 7

Amascut uses Devourer's Hieroglyphs in phase 7 alongside her standard shockwaves. These erupt after three ticks of charging and deal a large amount of defence-penetrating typeless damage.

Amascut will most likely be at low life points due to every shadow tear being absorbed, so it may be possible that hieroglyphs are not encountered.

If players cannot subdue Amascut before she recovers from her stagger, she will use a set of 4-6 hieroglyphs before repeating the Altar Strike special. Dodging them resets movement abilities, and there are always at least two areas that are not affected by them. Amascut is far more likely to use hieroglyphs over shockwaves, though both are possible to face.

Be aware of crocodiles and scarabs that may spawn depending on which of Tumeken's bau she calls upon.

These listed achievements are all part of the Combat subcategory Amascut and are all members-only.

Completing this achievement unlocks the title [Name], the Devoured.

## Requirements

There are 5 achievements in this group.

## Strategy

For a full strategy for each constituent achievement, see the page for that achievement. At 2000% enrage, players will be afflicted with the Lone Soul debuff, which prevents players from being affected by Intercept, Heal Other, and Heal Group. Most notably, this means that players cannot Intercept a teammate with Barricade or Immortality to avoid damage. As an overview of what specific actions players need to do in each phase:

• Phase 1
• Allow all the volatile scarabs to spawn
• Non-base tank players don't damage Amascut
• Phase 2
• Keep all 4 crocodiles alive until the end of the phase
• Pick up the fragments with under 30 seconds remaining, and click to deposit them with under 4.8 seconds remaining
• Nobody damages Amascut
• Phase 3
• Allow all the volatile scarabs to spawn
• Non-base tank players don't damage Amascut
• Phase 4
• Allow all the explosive scarabs to spawn - only walk around the edge of the arena during the whole phase
• Pick up the fragments with under 30 seconds remaining, and click to deposit them with under 4.8 seconds remaining
• Nobody damages Amascut
• Phase 5
• Damage Amascut to around 80% health
• Phase 6
• Do not damage the engulfing shadow
• Break the black bar shield or use Immortality to survive not breaking the shield
• Damage Amascut to just over 75% health (9,000,000)
• Phase 7
• Enter the phase with above 75% health (9,000,000)
• (If present) Do not kill any crocodiles that spawn
• If Amascut calls the Crondis statue, the team may choose to not provoke her toward it, so that the crocodiles do not spawn. However, this will cause all players to take a large hit of damage that must be mitigated.

infobox.Description: Defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 2000% enrage while completing the listed achievements.

achievements.name: Animal Cruelty
achievements.description: Have Durzag deal the killing blow to both Tuz and Krar.
achievements.wikiSummary: Animal Cruelty is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful fight against Beastmaster Durzag where both Tuz and Krar are killed by Durzag's attacks.
achievements.wikiText:
Animal Cruelty is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful fight against Beastmaster Durzag where both Tuz and Krar are killed by Durzag's attacks.

## Strategy

There are two main methods of letting the pets die to Durzag: Durzag himself or the bombs. Either method can be used, but if one pet dies to any player damage (this includes deflect damage and poison), then the achievement does not complete. Out of the two methods using the bombs is safer.

Each pet tank should keep both pets near 100,000 life points, by which time the rest of the team should be attacking Durzag. When Durzag is at 750,000 life points, it is necessary to kill the pets.

If using Durzag to deal the damage directly, the base tank should lure Durzag towards the pets and hope that his area-of-effect attacks kill the pets.

If using the bombs to deal the damage, most of the players should stand near Tuz and Krar so that when bombs are released, they are next to the pets. The 2,000 magic damage from a bomb can be avoided by activating Surge or Escape just before it detonates.

It may be helpful for pet tanks to be on the normal prayer book so that their deflect curses don't kill the pets. Furthermore, not using weapon poison or any deflect item such as a deathtouched bracelet is useful.

If you die and the rest of the team finishes the kill, you will still be complete the achievement if you re-enter the arena before the kill is finished.

infobox.Description: Have Durzag deal the killing blow to both Tuz and Krar.

achievements.name: Anti-anima-golem
achievements.description: Defeat Telos, the Warden at 100% or higher enrage without being hit by an anima-golem.
achievements.wikiSummary: Anti-anima-golem is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Telos, the Warden at 100% or higher enrage without being successfully hit by an anima-golem.
achievements.wikiText:
Anti-anima-golem is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Telos, the Warden at 100% or higher enrage without being successfully hit by an anima-golem.

## Strategy

Despite the achievement's in-game requirement, players are not disqualified from the task if the anima-golem attacks but fails to hit. However, they are very accurate to begin with, so it is best to not let them close the distance.

Anima-golems in phase 4 will spawn next to their corresponding font when Telos is phased accordingly to 25% of its health in that phase (at 100% enrage, this would mean at 93,750, 62,500 and 31,250 health). Try to bind the golems from afar and make note of the font timer, as failing to set up a shield in time will cause a soft instant kill. The pure and corrupt anima-golems have halberd range, while the volcanic anima-golems follow normal melee range.

At phase 5, the golems will generally spawn around the starting position, so using Surge and Dive should help cover a lot of distance. This should be done a few ticks after entering P5, as instant movement will result in the golems spawning where you have moved to. The volcanic golems in this phase will have halberd melee range.

The platypus pet can be used to slow golems down especially on phase 5 if you run around Telos in melee distance.

infobox.Description: Defeat Telos, the Warden at 100% or higher enrage without being hit by an anima-golem.

Araxxi Master Speed Killer is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Araxxi solo in less than 1 minute and 42 seconds.

This achievement can only be completed in a private instance.

## Strategy

This phase requires that the top path is opened, as the player has to wait a minute to burn the web to phase 2.

When taking the top path, players should dart straight to phase 3 without damaging Araxxor. Using a powerburst of acceleration can help reach phase 3 faster, then surge back to where Araxxor is. The player must deal 100,000 (or 80,000 with Necromancy's Death Mark) within 5 seconds, or Araxxor will be healed from the spiders above for large amounts of health.

The top path should be combined with the middle path, as Araxxi will prioritise acid absorption over minions during phase 4, and the player should have more than enough time to prevent minions from being called. This is especially important, as Araxxi's minions do not follow a set order compared to Araxxor's meaning that a mirrorback spider could potentially appear as the first spider regardless of set and likely get the player killed due to their high damage output.

achievements.wikiText:
Avaryss' Avarice is an achievement that requires the player to defeat the Twin Furies in a solo encounter without being hit by Avaryss, the Unceasing's Surge attack.

At the beginning of the fight, Avaryss, the Unceasing will use this ability four times, charging towards her target from each different direction one time. The pattern is northern wall heading south, western wall heading east, southern wall heading north, and finally eastern wall heading west. She covers a 3-tile wide path when she charges. Move out of her path every time. After the Lava Bomb ability, the Twin Furies will restart their attack cycle and four more surges will need to be dodged.

## Strategy

Pick the side that does not have Torag the Corrupted, even if said side contains both Karil the Tainted and Ahrim the Blighted. Obtaining War's Blessing 3 grants the ability to choose specific rotations.

Weaken the brothers on the selected side to around 10,000 life points and wait for the remaining three brothers on the other side to cross over. Afterwards, immediately begin killing the brothers, starting with Karil the Tainted and Torag the Corrupted. Karil the Tainted will severely limit accessible space, while getting hammered by Torag the Corrupted will result in a restart as players cannot attack while being pummeled. Using area-of-effect abilities will help deal significant damage to the brothers. The melee brothers cannot attack the player with proper running, but this will drain a lot of run energy, especially if the player's damage output is poor. This can be circumvented by visiting the salt-water spring for unlimited run energy for a short time.

## Strategy

This achievement must be done with a team, since during solo attempts the brothers will not move to the other side until about 24 seconds into the fight.

Each brother has 50,000 hitpoints and will spawn in front of the portal when the fight initiates.

Ideally, the rotation should consist of one ranged brother (Ahrim, Karil) on each side, with the remaining two brothers being melee (Torag, Guthan, Verac, Dharok). If two ranged brothers are on the same side, obtaining the achievement will be a lot harder as it is not possible to AoE them effectively. Death-dot on the ranged brother and use all AoE abilities possible. Using combat dummies to prebuild is helpful for immediate damage. Death Mark can also be used, instantly killing the brother after they fall below 10,000 health with Necromancy attacks.

## Strategy

Solo Durzag is considered an extreme step up and requires use of unorthodox methods to finish the fight.

During the pre-waves, avoid being combo'ed out by the airut, chargers and Cormes.

After the pre-waves are cleared, Durzag will spawn to the northeast alongside either Tuz or Krar. Stand near the west gate, let the pet aggro and then kill it. If Durzag aggros alongside the pet, it is recommended to reset.

Once the pet is killed, aggro Durzag and continually run in a straight line back and forth. As long as Durzag is not given the chance to use melee until he reaches half health, the third pet will never appear. If done correctly, the pet should not appear, he will not be able to release the chargers and will only use ranged attacks. If this pet does appear, reset.

Beetlejuice Beetlejuice is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful Kalphite King encounter in a team of four or fewer without anyone dying to a "Beetlejuice" attack.

When one player is affected by the attack and stunned, another player should Provoke and use a defensive such as Resonance or Disruption Shield. A safer alternative is to Deflect Melee and use Devotion as minions may hit the player before Kalphite King does, removing those abilities as options to mitigate the Beetlejuice attack.

Skipping the mechanic altogether will also trigger the achievement.

achievements.name: Before You Go Aken
achievements.description: Defeat TzKal-Zuk in hard mode in a single run without letting TzekHaar-Aken submerge in wave 17.
achievements.wikiSummary: Before You Go Aken is an achievement that requires the player to defeat TzKal-Zuk in hard mode in a single run without letting TzekHaar-Aken submerge in wave 17.
achievements.wikiText:
Before You Go Aken is an achievement that requires the player to defeat TzKal-Zuk in hard mode in a single run without letting TzekHaar-Aken submerge in wave 17.

## Strategy

TzekHaar-Aken has 300,000 health in hard mode, and its head will immediately appear to the east or west once the wave starts. Necromancy has the easiest time in killing TzekHaar-Aken, as Death Mark can be used to immediately kill it once it falls below 30,000 health. It is still possible with other styles, but requires more timing.

TzekHaar-Aken will defend itself with magic and ranged tentacles; the magic tentacles give it damage reduction, but because they spawn randomly across the arena, it is best to ignore them. It will also launch lava at the player once in a while, and it is important to avoid these, as not only do they deal moderate damage, they also halve adrenaline gain, which can prevent crucial abilities from being used.

infobox.Description: Defeat TzKal-Zuk in hard mode in a single run without letting TzekHaar-Aken submerge in wave 17.

achievements.name: Best Offence
achievements.description: Defeat the Kalphite King after triggering his Immortality and then defeat him again.
achievements.wikiSummary: Best Offence is an achievement that requires the player to defeat the Kalphite King after his Immortality has been triggered, and then defeating him again.
achievements.wikiText:
Best Offence is an achievement that requires the player to defeat the Kalphite King after his Immortality has been triggered, and then defeating him again.

The Kalphite King will use Immortality when below 35,000 hitpoints and certain abilities are used on him depending on which phase he is in. The Kalphite King has a 20% chance upon being struck by the ability in the correct phase of activating Immortality, in which case it will last for 30 seconds.

• Magic phase: Bombardment
• Ranged phase: Pulverise
• Melee phase: Tsunami

Unlike Barricade, the King's Immortality does not have an animation; rather, a message box will appear stating The Kalphite King has activated Immortality! if it does trigger. Players must defeat the King within that time frame or it will expire and players will have to trigger it again. If doing the achievement in a group, only the player who activates Immortality will see the message, but all players will still be eligible for the achievement. Coordinate who will be attempting to activate Immortality and have the other watch the other closely, looking at the attack animations or adrenaline going down to attempt to kill the king after the Immortality.

Ideally, the player should bring both Necromancy and their desired combat style and swaps to perform the abilities on the other two styles not being used to minimise downtime waiting for an ideal combat form, applying Death Mark at the start of the kill. Drop the King to around 30,000 health and use the trigger ability when ideal. If the Immortality message appears, immediately swap to the necromancy weapon and use a necromancy ability so it triggers Death Mark. This is much faster than using another combat style and avoids the potential of a healing shield, which will cause the status to expire.

## Trivia

• The achievement name is a reference to the saying "The best defence is a good offence", encouraging proactive attacks in order to hinder an enemy's ability to effectively launch their own offence.

infobox.Description: Defeat the Kalphite King after triggering his Immortality and then defeat him again.

achievements.wikiText:
Better Not Touch is an achievement that requires the player participate in a successful battle against Yakamaru with all but one member of the party still under the effect of poison when he dies.

## Strategy

On the last phase before the mirage phase, the whole team should absorb the poison. North or base tank should lure Yakamaru with the poison, and the rest of the team must constantly stay at high life points as they take 500–1,000 poison damage every other game tick (every 1.2 seconds).

If the player that lured Yakamaru with the poison is killed or any dead players remain in the group when Yakamaru dies, the achievement will not complete.

## Trivia

• The achievement's name is a reference to the lyrics from the Alice Cooper song "Poison".

Trying to take the attack normally is highly discouraged, as the rockfall will always be positioned around the player's location and is very erratic, which can make it extremely hard to dodge when Graardor is also attacking at the same time. Instead, the player should kite Graardor from afar, as he will not be able to use any special attacks if he cannot reach the player.

Blade Dancer is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Gregorovic in a solo encounter without being hit by his Glaives attack.

## Strategy

Glaives is the special attack that follows shortly after Gregorovic summons a spirit from the nearby plinths. This attack is indicated with him throwing his glaives in the air, after which shadows will appear throughout the arena. Despite their 1x1 area of effect, the shadows actually have a 2x2 area of effect with the northern, north-eastern, and eastern tiles of the shadow being unsafe, so players should avoid these tiles. The achievement will also complete if the player kills Gregorovic before he gets a chance to use it.

achievements.name: Bleed Tank
achievements.description: Defeat Vorago with only one person ever being the target of the 'Destroy Tank' attack during the 'Vitalis Bomb' stage.
achievements.wikiSummary: Bleed Tank is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Vorago with only one player ever being the target of the "Destroy Tank" attack during the "Vitalis Bomb" phase.
achievements.wikiText:
Bleed Tank is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Vorago with only one player ever being the target of the "Destroy Tank" attack during the "Vitalis Bomb" phase.

## Strategy

Vorago can use his "Destroy Tank" bleed attack during phase 3 when on Vitalis rotation in normal mode, and during phase 5 in hard mode.

This achievement requires that Vorago uses his bleed attack during this phase, and that only one player is ever targeted by it. Unlike many of the other Vorago achievements, skipping this mechanic will not award the achievement.

Vorago's attack rotation during Vitalis is:

• Vitalis orb
• 3 auto-attacks
• Reflect
• 3 auto-attacks
• Vitalis orb
• 3 auto-attacks
• Destroy Tank
• 3 auto-attacks
• Repeats

By default, all players are ineligible for this achievement, and it requires Vorago to use his bleed attack at least once during the Vitalis Bomb phase for the message You are now eligible for: Bleed Tank to appear. If after that a second player gets targetted by a bleed, the message You have failed: Bleed Tank appears and the achievement is no longer awarded.

Try to bring Vorago to at least 40,000 life points with Death Mark, and wait for the Destroy Tank animation and eligibility prompt to appear before clearing the phase.

## Achievement set

Completing this achievement in a hard mode Vorago instance is one of the requirements for the Vorago (HM) (unorthodox) grandmaster achievement.

## Strategy

By maintaining a high damage output, Solak will automatically transition to phase 3 if his phase 2 "health" pool meets the transition threshold. Teams should be able to obtain this before the first Blight Barrage. If they cannot achieve this in time, Barricade is mandatory to survive the onslaught, as the barrage will deal five hits of up to 8,000 damage.

Blight the Way with Eruptions is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Solak, Guardian of the Grove after dealing with all eruptions within 6 seconds of each other.

## Strategy

All players should handle each anima eruption accordingly to team size. This is best done in a group of 4, as to avoid excessive damage and dispelling an eruption too quickly. Each player should go to a different corner and DPS their respective eruption down.

As the intended way to clear the anima storm is to be cleansed before going up to dispel it with one eruption at a time, the team will be continually pelted by the anima storm throughout the fight. Players should watch their health to ensure that its blasts and Solak's attacks do not kill them.

achievements.description: Defeat Nex, Angel of Death in a team of 7 or fewer after placing each 'Mark of the Elements' in the center of the arena.
achievements.wikiSummary: Bomb disposal unit is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Nex, Angel of Death in a team of 7 or fewer after placing each 'Mark of the Elements' in the center of the arena.
achievements.wikiText:
Bomb disposal unit is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Nex, Angel of Death in a team of 7 or fewer after placing each 'Mark of the Elements' in the center of the arena.

As Mark of the Elements occurs constantly from the point when Nex reaches 600,000 life points, players should do as much damage as possible to reduce the number of bombs encountered in this phase.

It is recommended that a player spends as little time as possible in the centre of the arena to mitigate as much damage as possible. This means using Surge or Dive as late as possible as the bar is filling up. Furthermore, defensive abilities such as Debilitate and Reflect or Barricade can mitigate the soft typeless damage.

Every player is eligible for this achievement once the fight starts and becomes ineligible once a bomb is placed outside of the centre of the arena. A Sign of life activation on the first loading bar will prevent the bomb from spawning; this does not disqualify players from the achievement. This can be a useful strategy, especially for slower teams, so fewer bombs (or no bombs) have to be placed in the middle of the arena.

achievements.name: Bring the Roof Down, But Not On Me
achievements.wikiTitle: Bring the Roof Down, But Not On Me
achievements.description: Defeat Vorago without anyone being hit by any falling rocks during the 'Ceiling Collapse' stage.
achievements.wikiSummary: Bring the Roof Down, But Not On Me is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Vorago without anyone being hit by any falling rocks during the "Ceiling Collapse" attack.
achievements.wikiText:
Bring the Roof Down, But Not On Me is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Vorago without anyone being hit by any falling rocks during the "Ceiling Collapse" attack.

## Strategy

Vorago can use his Ceiling Collapse attack during phases 3 and 4 in normal mode, but only when the rotation is Ceiling Collapse. Despite the description, it is also required to interact with this mechanic when it appears in phase 4. In hard mode, the Ceiling Collapse attack occurs in phase 3, and also in phase 9 if the rotation is set to Ceiling Collapse.

This achievement requires that every time Vorago uses his Ceiling Collapse, no player takes damage from it. Shadows will appear on the ground where the rocks will fall before the damage is dealt, so that players can see where to avoid standing. The area of the damage is slightly larger than the shadows, so stand a good distance away to be sure. It is recommended to clear the fallen debris so that movement for later rocks is not impeded.

By default, all players are eligible for this achievement, and it is only once any player takes damage from the falling rocks that the message You have failed: Bring the Roof Down, But Not On Me appears and the achievement is no longer awarded. Thus completing a kill where one or more Ceiling Collapse mechanics are skipped, such as by ending phase 3 before the second Ceiling Collapse happens, will not invalidate the achievement.

## Achievement set

Completing this achievement in a hard mode Vorago instance is one of the requirements for the Vorago (HM) (perfect) grandmaster achievement.

## Strategy

Kalphite King will burrow in his magic and ranged forms. Kalphite King will burrow into the ground after a set interval, indicated with him leaping into the ground. Shortly afterwards, his horn will appear underneath his main target before he bursts up, knocking anyone in a 5-by-5 area underneath him.

The burrow can be skipped in his magic form with a stun, but the ranged dig can only be skipped if he is prompted to summon minions. However, it is still best to avoid stuns completely, since they can mess up his attack rotation and make him burrow twice in a row.

achievements.name: Calculated
achievements.description: Defeat Vorago without anyone activating any of the magic and explosive bombs during the 'The End' stage.
achievements.wikiSummary: Calculated is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Vorago without anyone activating any of the magic or explosive bombs during the "The End" attacks.
achievements.wikiText:
Calculated is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Vorago without anyone activating any of the magic or explosive bombs during the "The End" attacks.

## Strategy

Vorago can use his "The End" attack during phases 3 and 4 in normal mode, but only when the rotation is The End. Despite the description, it is also required to interact with this mechanic when it appears in phase 4. In hard mode, The End occurs in phase 8, and also in phase 9 if the rotation is The End.

This achievement requires that every time Vorago uses The End, none of the blue magic bombs or red explosive bombs are released before he finishes the attack. This means that all of the bombs will be released onto random players when the attack finishes. The magic bombs deal magic damage and the explosive bombs deal typeless damage and deactivate defensive abilities. To mitigate this damage, players should spread out to avoid overlap and use non-defensive damage mitigation such as magic prayer, a powerburst of vitality, and Shield Dome.

By default, all players are eligible for this achievement, and it is only once a bomb is released during a The End attack that the message You have failed: Calculated appears and the achievement is no longer awarded. Thus completing a kill where phase 3 (or 8 in hard mode) is ended before The End attack finishes will not invalidate the achievement, as long as no bombs were released.

This requires Zamorak's green health bar to be cleared prior to him making a second attack. The achievement will be failed if he begins to cast the special attack, even though phase six could end prior to the special attack actually landing.

## Strategy

Zamorak will not perform any special attacks during his grey health bar phase, so it is highly recommended to lower this health bar as much as possible before activating a rune pad, minimising the amount of damage required for this achievement. Before activating a rune pad, prepare for a high-damage ability rotation. As soon as a rune pad is activated, players will have around 10 seconds to deal the required amount of damage to transition Zamorak into his next grey health bar phase.

It is recommended to activate the H rune last, as this rune will trigger Coven hex causing both a Protector and Lifeweaver to spawn if they are within minimap range of the player. The player can stand to the east, thereby only causing the lifeweaver to make an action while the protector remains idle. The protector will provide Zamorak with a 25% damage reduction if she makes an action, which makes damaging Zamorak much more tedious.

achievements.name: Canon Event
achievements.description: Defeat Kerapac, the bound in hard mode, solo with at least 3 active time thread tears.
achievements.wikiSummary: Canon Event is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Kerapac, the bound in solo hard mode encounter with at least three active time thread tears.
achievements.wikiText:
Canon Event is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Kerapac, the bound in solo hard mode encounter with at least three active time thread tears.

## Strategy

Kerapac summons one time thread tear per player every time he uses his Shatter special attack, as long as the player does not stand underneath Kerapac. The tear is sent in a line from Kerapac, through the player, to reach one of the edges of the arena. Thus, it is possible to control where the tears spawn by where the player stands relative to Kerapac. It is recommended to place the tears in locations safely away from any other enemy the player may wish to fight, such as in the north east or south east corners. During phase 4, echoes of Kerapac spawn to the north, west, and south, and Kerapac himself is in the east, so these cardinal directions are not recommended.

Players need to be careful as each active thread will deal around 500 soft typeless damage every few ticks, which will quickly add up in phase 4 when damage and survivability is required. Defensive abilities such as Reflect can be used to mitigate damage, but the tears are not immune to reflect damage and can potentially die from them. They are also susceptible to poison and players should avoid bringing cinderbane gloves or weapon poison for this achievement.

An efficient kill will only allow Kerapac to use his Shatter special attack once per phase, so this achievement would involve allowing all Shatter specials to produce a tear, and killing none of them.

### Alternative strategy

An alternative strategy is to avoid the time thread tears being summoned during phases 1 and 2, by standing under Kerapac during the Shatter special attack, and then stalling the kill during phase 3 to have him summon three time threads all in phase 3. You can use the special action button in combination with defensive abilities such as Barricade to mitigate the damage during phase 3 while you wait for three rotations to occur. Once three time thread tears have spawned, finish the kill as normal being sure to not accidentally kill any of the time thread tears.

## Achievement set

If this achievement is completed in the same kill as One At a Time and Pruning the Timeline, it will award the Kerapac, the bound (unorthodox) grandmaster achievement.

## Trivia

• The achievement's name is a reference to Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse, where canon events are events that must occur in order to shape the lives of the various Spider-People across the multiverse.

## Strategy

Shadow anima pools should be eliminated during the transition from phase 2 to 3, as this is the last time they appear during the encounter. It is important to take them out regardless, since they will restore Raksha's health alongside increasing his damage and defence reduction. While this can be done using necromancy abilities such as Threads of Fate or Bloat, the most reliable method is wearing laceration boots along with a two-handed weapon such as Laniakea's spear or a noxious scythe and using the Bladed Dive ability as successful hits on the pools will reset the ability's cooldown, allowing players to clear all pools back-to-back. When doing this, it is important to target the pool furthest away from the player as they move between sets to ensure all pools are cleared consistently.

achievements.description: Defeat the Ambassador without destroying any sinister fragments.
achievements.wikiSummary: Clenched is an achievement that requires the player to defeat The Ambassador inside The Shadow Reef without destroying any sinister fragments.
achievements.wikiText:
Clenched is an achievement that requires the player to defeat The Ambassador inside The Shadow Reef without destroying any sinister fragments.

This achievement can only be completed in normal mode.

## Strategy

It is strongly recommended to attempt this achievement in a group because of the length of the fight for solo players. The attack is forced at 650,000 health if the Ambassador has not used this attack once. Prior to the spawning of the fragments, target the Ambassador with Soul Split; though he does not take any damage, Soul Split will still heal as normal. Damaging the fragments is optional (as the achievement states that they must not be destroyed, not that they can't be damaged), but it is ill-advised as weapon poison may accidentally destroy them.

As all six fragments must remain intact, this means players will receive six shockwave attacks. It is strongly recommended to gain 100% adrenaline during the spawn of the fragments as well as full health. To survive the barrage of explosions the Ambassador unleashes, use the following rotation:

• After the Ambassador absorbs the fragments: Cast Enfeeble to weaken the damage of each explosion by 10%.
• First explosion: Equip a shield and use Resonance after the Ambassador's auto-attack attack registers on the player. If players are concerned with this attack sniping Resonance, use Devotion and pray accordingly before using Resonance.
• Second and third explosions: Debilitate with a tier 90 shield prior to the second explosion. Reflect may be used to decrease the damage by 75%, though the explosion will deal roughly 3,900-4,200 damage otherwise. If only one of the abilities is used to deal with an explosion, then players can tank the second, third and fourth explosions with these two abilities at the cost of eating more food.
• Fourth and fifth explosions: Use Barricade. The Turtling perk can extend Barricade's duration. If the fourth explosion was tanked with Debilitate/Reflect, then Barricade can tank the final two explosions.
• Sixth fragment: Depending on adrenaline and available abilities, it is possible just eat to full health and tank the damage. Shield Dome is also an option depending on spellbook, as is Disruption Shield.
• Additional notes: If the player struggles to survive the hits, they may also bring along a divine, arcane, elysian or spectral spirit shield with a penance powder to absorb as much damage as possible decreasing the overall threat of the fragments, as with the shields, it eliminates the need to spend adrenaline on barricade, allowing the player to throw out more damaging abilities making the fight smoother.
• Powerburst of vitality can help if the player runs out of defensive options.
• Limitless can help reduce the need for 50% adrenaline in a pinch.
• Immortality can be used as a last resort once every attack cycle.

A combination of Barricade and Intercept can also be used between each player in the group. One player uses Barricade and intercepts the other two players for two fragments, then the responsibility rotates to the next two players for the remaining four fragments. However, this can be difficult to coordinate.

If attempting the achievement solo, using a Beast of Burden or a blood reaver with sufficient Prism of Restoration usage is recommended. Before the first beam attack, the Ambassador should be damaged as much as possible with a good Sunshine rotation. To deal with the shockwaves, the above rotation can still be followed. However, using Sunshine near the tail-end of each beam attack is highly recommended, as without it, it is very difficult to do enough damage between the required defensives to progress the fight. The optimal timing for the Sunshine would give enough time to build up the adrenaline by attacking the Ambassador to cast the above rotation. To aid in the timing, the player may right click mark on the sinister fragment closest to them in the clockwise direction and then pay attention to when they meet up again with it going around in the counter-clockwise direction.

## Strategy

Initiate the ice phase by phasing Nex after she attempts to use Blood Sacrifice on the player. This will cause her to use Contain as her first special attack rather than Ice Prison, the latter of which will cause an immediate fail if it occurs. Try to maintain some distance from Nex so the icicles from her Contain attack do not reach as this will also fail the achievement, and keep Protect/Deflect Magic on during this attack to avoid getting frozen.

Nex will sometimes melee the player during this phase, so the player should take advantage of this by kiting her. Nex will eventually stop once she realises she is unable to use melee, returning to magic attacks. Players with Necromancy or Ranged can use Split Soul or the eldritch crossbow variant to deal additional damage, which is especially helpful to kill Glacies due to her 1,000 damage soft cap and 2,000 damage hard cap.

achievements.wikiText:
Comeback kid is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Vorago after being pushed close to the edge of the arena in the final phase.

## Strategy

Vorago has a unique damage mechanic in phase 5 in normal mode and 10/11 in hard mode where he moves forward and backward depending on the amounts of damage done to him and done by him to players. As he damages players he moves forwards, and as players damage him he moves backward. Some forms of damage mitigation can prevent him from moving forward, and making him move backward briefly delays his next attack.

This achievement requires players to let Vorago push them all the way back to the last possible square that they may stand on, before damaging Vorago sufficiently to push him all the way to the other end of the arena and winning the fight. Players must not take any pushback when on the last possible square or else the pushback will fail the encounter, see the push mechanics table. It is recommended that one player use Intercept and Barricade so the other players may focus on dealing damage. Disruption Shield may be used but will only block one attack, and Devotion can prevent pushback when combined with the correct protection prayers. It is also important to time Vorago's attack rotation so that he does not use destroy tank or reflect as the team reaches the last possible square, since the latter ignores defensives (especially if a player is targeted twice) and the former will prevent the team from pushing and causes him to pushback if any damage is reflected.

By default all players are ineligible for this achievement, and as Vorago moves closer to the front of the arena the message You have progressed toward: Comeback kid appears. Once the final tile is reached, the message becomes You are now eligible for: Comeback kid, and the fight should be continued.

Connection lost. Please wait - attempting to reestablish is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Rasial, the First Necromancer without moving for 45 seconds after being hit by his 'Finger of Death' attack in phase 4.

## Strategy

Despite the achievement's description, the Finger of Death the game refers to is not the Necromancy ability itself; rather, it is the eruptions that appear under the player.

The achievement begins tracking in the player's chatbox as soon as the player is hit by one of these eruptions. These will deal up to 4,500 necromancy damage, but can be mitigated with defensive abilities and prayers/curses. During the phase, Rasial will also use his prayer-disabling attack alongside the eruptions, so players should keep their health very high.

Players should use the following to tank the eruptions for 45 seconds:

• Combine Anticipation with Devotion (full protection for 10 seconds)
• Freedom (allows for protection prayers/curses for 6 seconds)
• Debilitate
• Reflect
• Shield Dome
• Barricade with a tier 90 shield, provides 10.2 seconds of immunity
• With Turtling 4, 13.2 seconds of immunity
• With Turtling 4 and two Malletops perks from the Anachronia Dinosaur Farm, 17.4 seconds of immunity
• Immortality (reduces incoming damage by 25% while active, revives if player health falls below 0 in this time with 1.8 seconds of immunity)
• Powerburst of vitality
• Hellhound familiar
• Eat food
• Enfeeble
• Sign of life or equivalent
• Ring of death (last resort)

## Trivia

• The name of this achievement is the same as the message that shows when a player's game client loses connection to the game's servers.

achievements.wikiText:
Cormes and Goes is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful fight against Beastmaster Durzag where Cormes is left alive.

## Strategy

This achievement is relatively simple and can be accomplished simultaneously with other achievements. Cormes spawns during the wave of monsters before Beastmaster Durzag spawns. When he spawns, one person should be a designated tank and stay on the western side of the arena. Simply provoke, equip a shield, and tank all damage until Beastmaster Durzag is dead. No player should be dealing damage to Cormes (besides the tank in small amounts).

Like other pets, Cormes can jump to other nearby players. It is important that the tank provokes Cormes back on them and lures them to the side so that he doesn't attack any other players.

## Trivia

• This achievement's name is a play on the phrase "comes and goes".
• This feat was previously known as "One more couldn't hurt..."
• The world-first broadcast during the Equilibrium League still used the old name.

Crassian en Masse is an achievement that requires the player to defeat the Sanctum Guardian in the Temple of Aminishi with exactly 10 Crassian reinforcements still alive.

This achievement cannot be completed in Story Mode.

Crassian reinforcements are only sent after every four torrent attacks. This means that the player(s) must be prepared to survive at least 20 torrents and 20 smoke patches.

Use of the Barricade ability allows the player to stack the smoke patches on top of each other without immediately dying, reducing the overall spread of the smoke patches over a lengthened period of time.

Protect from Missiles should be considered over Deflect Missiles, as there is a real risk that the deflection might finish off the first Crassians by the time 10 are summoned.

This is done when Seiryu the Azure Serpent appears and destroys the crassians. The achievement is completed as soon as the crassians are killed; defeating the Ambassador is not required. It can be completed in both normal mode and story mode. After completing this achievement, the player may purchase the Tetch pet from the Daemonheim Rewards shop for 250,000 dungeoneering tokens.
achievements.wikiText:
Crawfish Boil is an achievement that requires the player to disintegrate 12 crassian ritual keepers simultaneously during the Ambassador encounter inside the Shadow Reef. This is done when Seiryu the Azure Serpent appears and destroys the crassians. The achievement is completed as soon as the crassians are killed; defeating the Ambassador is not required. It can be completed in both normal mode and story mode. After completing this achievement, the player may purchase the Tetch pet from the Daemonheim Rewards shop for 250,000 dungeoneering tokens.

The number of ritual keepers that spawn is based on the group's size - for the fastest results, fight Kranon in a group of three. This means that he only needs to spawn three sets of ritual keepers to meet the achievement's requirements. Do not damage Kranon below 200,000 (story mode) or 400,000 (normal mode) health until twelve ritual keepers are in the arena. In story mode, it is advised to wait until Seiryu heals and disintegrates the keepers as phasing to the final phase prematurely forces Seiryu to spawn but does not unlock the achievement. If opting to complete in normal mode, players can build adrenaline on the crassians to use defensives and stall time while waiting for enough crassian spawns, as attempting to build adrenaline on the Ambassador will likely phase him prematurely. If opting to complete in a group, it is possible to kill the Ambassador too quickly before Seiryu destroys the crassians, which will not complete the achievement. Be sure to slow down and let the achievement complete before focusing on the Ambassador.

## Trivia

• The name is how crayfish are cooked in real life; this is reflected by Seiryu's fire destroying the arthropod-like crassians.

Day at the Aquarium is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful battle against Yakamaru where a Durable and a Reflecting Jellyfish are kept alive and within range of Yakamaru's attacks when he dies.

## Strategies

Both Durable Jellyfish and Reflecting Jellyfish need to be within range of Yakamaru's attacks when Yakamaru dies for the achievement to complete. Leave the jellyfish alive after they spawn after poisoning Yakamaru in the third and fourth pools, respectively. Upon the Reflecting Jellyfish appearing, leave one Piercing Jellyfish alive or the Reflecting Jellyfish will be killed as a result. The three jellyfish can be lured far north or far south so that area-of-effect attacks by the team do not accidentally kill the remaining jellyfish or the Durable Jellyfish. As the last mirage pool is being closed up, have the team wait for the jellyfish to be lured near Yakamaru, then have the team finish the kill. Do not let the durable jellyfish come too close to Yakamaru, or he will consume the jellyfish and fully heal himself, starting Rewind.

## Strategy

When Beastmaster Durzag appears, no player should open any of the small cages on the walls of the arena. Players should be aware when the cages automatically open after 20–30 seconds of Durzag appearing, and all 24 chargers rush at players simultaneously. Protecting from melee will be useful. ## Strategy

Much like Healing for Days, players will not fail the achievement if the corrupted scarab healer reaches Nakatra; rather, it must be killed before its bar fills. Stuns are required in order to damage the scarabs.

Scarabs will appear during phase 1 if Nakatra is allowed to perform a second set of ranged attacks, also indicated with the third use of the Soulfire Waves attack.

In phase 2, they will appear in the second instance of the Soulfire Waves attack.

Players with strong damage output should be able to prevent scarabs from appearing at all in normal mode, and at least the set in phase 1 in hard mode.

## Trivia

• The name of the achievement is a reference to the quest Dealing with Scabaras.

achievements.name: Dedicated Denial of Standing (here)
achievements.description: Defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 1000% or higher enrage without anyone being hit by her 'Empowered Soulfire', 'Devourer's Shockwave' and 'Devourer's Hieroglyphs' attacks.
achievements.wikiSummary: Dedicated Denial of Standing (here) is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 1,000% or higher enrage without anyone being hit by her 'Empowered Soulfire', 'Devourer's Shockwave' and 'Devourer's Hieroglyphs' attacks.
achievements.wikiText:
Dedicated Denial of Standing (here) is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 1,000% or higher enrage without anyone being hit by her 'Empowered Soulfire', 'Devourer's Shockwave' and 'Devourer's Hieroglyphs' attacks.

## Requirements

This achievement requires that no player in the group is hit by any of the telegraphed floor area attacks throughout the entire fight. They are present in phases 2, 3, 4, and 7. It also requires that the enrage of the fight is at least 1000%, although completing it at 2000% is one of the requirements for the perfect achievement.

Empowered Soulfire are the waves of fire in phases 2 and 4 that travel south-to-north on the main arena while someone is carrying a fragment of Tumeken. They are also present in the side rooms for Crondis (East side, phase 2) and Scabaras (West side, phase 4).

Devourer's Shockwaves are the expanding square ring attacks that are used by Amascut in phases 3 and 7. They are also present in the side rooms for Apmeken (West side, phase 2) and Het (East side, phase 4).

Devourer's Hieroglyphs are only present in phase 7, and are the large square attacks in a 3x3 grid that she uses while she is attackable. This special attack is identical to that of Nakatra in Sanctum of Rebirth.

This achievement is failed if any player is hit by one of the aforementioned attacks, even if the damage is blocked by Barricade. The message You have failed: Dedicated Denial of Standing (here): <Player> was hit by <Mechanic> is displayed if any player is hit.

## Strategy

Careful movement and knowledge of the upcoming floor patterns is required to complete this achievement. At 2000% enrage, the floor patterns change at a faster speed than at lower enrages.

### Side Rooms

The shockwave side rooms, Apmeken and Het, have their chains in positions that can be safe-spotted from areas not targeted by shockwaves, so long as the player are using Ranged or Magic for the longer attack range. The soulfire side rooms, Crondis and Scabaras, the side chains can only be safespotted from the far edges of the room, which requires travel through the non-safe areas to reach them. Alternatively, ranged or magic can reach the chains from the area around the center of the T-shaped walkway, which minimises movement required to avoid the waves.

In both cases, familiarisation with the order in which the different patterns occur is advised, especially when travelling to and from the center of the room to pick up the fragment of Tumeken.

### Carrying fragments of Tumeken

Players carrying fragments of Tumeken from the side rooms to the statues cannot use Surge, Escape, or Dive to speed up their movement. They must cross the soulfire waves without being hit, including the first soulfire wave after exiting the side room. The player carrying the fragment should communicate with their team to leave the side room at a time when they will not be hit by the first soulfire wave. The remaining waves alternate between two patterns, which allows for temporary safety as the patterns wait to change.

The soulfire waves start when a player leaves a side room carrying a fragment, and waves fire every 3 seconds, or 5 ticks. This allows players to travel up to 10 tiles between waves, and each soufire wave is 9 tiles wide. This allows players to safely travel across the arena with out being hit by waves, by timing their movement to start travelling across the area covered by a wave as soon as it passes, and then repeating for the next wave area. The exception to this is the central area, where there are two waves next to each other, and the alternating pattern wave overlaps on the same space. This requires travelling 14 tiles in 5 ticks, which is impossible with running alone. Instead, players may use the fact that Amascut only throws out 5 sets of waves, which means that waves no longer spawn 18 seconds after they start. Since carrying a fragment has a 30 second timer, this means that players must be very efficient in their movement to complete carrying the fragment in time.

Players carrying fragments can also use Barge or Prism of Salvation to speed up their movement. Barge requires a melee weapon and a target, which can be achieved by a team member luring one of the various Akh into a favourable position. Prisms can be placed by team members ahead of time, however care should be taken as the precise tile on which a player ends up by using a prism varies, depending on where they were when they clicked the prism. With careful placing and timing, prisms can be used to cross the central area without needing to wait for the soulfire waves to completely stop.

### Phase 3 shockwaves

The shockwaves in wave 3 should be avoided as per usual, with minimal disruption to attack rotations by walking back and forth 1 tile across the boundary between two shockwave zones.

### Phase 7

Hieroglyphs in phase 7 should be avoided by making use of the fact that movement abilities have their cooldown reset when successfully avoiding them. At 1,000 enrage, the cyan areas affected by the hieroglyphs charge at the same speed as the ones found in the hard mode version of the Nakatra, Devourer Eternal fight, in addition to being the same patterns.

At 2,000 enrage, hieroglyphs erupt one tick quicker, giving players three ticks to move to a safe area.

The shockwaves in phase 7 function the same as those on phase 3, and players should move to the parts of the ring that are not expanding.

Mitigating damage from Amascut's triple style-specific attack is not necessary to earn the achievement.

## Achievement Set

Completing this achievement at 2000% enrage is one of the requirements for the Amascut, the Devourer (perfect) grandmaster achievement.

## Trivia

• The name is a reference to the term "distributed denial-of-service attack" or "DDoS attack" which is a cyberattack that involves disrupting services by flooding the targeted machine or resource with superfluous requests in an attempt to overload it.

Definitely Can't Touch This is an achievement that requires the player to complete a Kerapac, the bound encounter in hard mode without getting hit by his "Lightning Strike" attack.

## Strategy

The Lightning Strike attack occurs as the third mechanic Kerapac uses in his attack rotation, and can be skipped with sufficient damage output, which will complete the achievement. This achievement can be completed in a duo or trio encounter.

If the player or group does not skip the attack and prevent the lightning walls from appearing, then they may be avoided by careful use of Dive and Surge to pass over them without being hit. Care is needed as the lightning walls have a larger area of effect than their visual appearance, and can be very difficult in phase 3 as there are three walls which come from different directions.

## Achievement set

If this achievement is completed in a solo hard mode kill alongside Shatterproof, Ready, Set, Go!, and Working With Myself, it will award the Kerapac, the bound (perfect) grandmaster achievement.

achievements.wikiText:
Did It For Them is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Nex, Angel of Death in a team of 7 or fewer without allowing any of the unstable smoke crystals to explode.

## Strategy

This attack is launched during phase 3, after Nex has reached 1,800,000 health. When the attack is initiated, she will send a cloud of smoke at a random direction. Standing within this cloud will cause an unstable smoke crystal to appear.

There is a 1/3 chance for this attack to be used, as it shares the same slots as her ice prison and smoke walls mechanics.

After the larger smoke field appears, players have a few seconds before the crystal explodes. If a player prematurely grabs the crystal, it will damage anyone within the cloud's range for 14,000 hard typeless damage. This will also reset any defensive abilities. At minimum, two players would need over 7,000 health to survive the blast, but it is best to hover around 9,000 health to account for Nex's attacks.

If one player is taking the crystal alone, a powerburst of vitality is necessary. Alternatively, less effective methods include bringing a tier 90 shield, a set of tier 80 or 90 deathwarden robe armour, overhealing with rocktail or sailfish products and a bonfire boost, though this is more required for tier 80 deathwarden.

infobox.Description: Defeat Nex, Angel of Death in a team of 7 or fewer without allowing any of the 'Unstable Smoke' crystals to explode.

achievements.name: Did you feel that?
achievements.description: Defeat the Queen Black Dragon after surviving a full time stop special attack.
achievements.wikiSummary: Did you feel that? is an achievement that requires the player to defeat the Queen Black Dragon after surviving a full time stop special attack.
achievements.wikiText:
Did you feel that? is an achievement that requires the player to defeat the Queen Black Dragon after surviving a full time stop special attack.

## Time stop attack

During phase 2 and 3, the Queen Black Dragon will manifest tortured souls as part of her special attacks.

In phase 4, if at least one tortured soul is alive, she will execute the "time stop" attack. One of the souls will shout Kill me mortal...quickly! HURRY! BEFORE THE SPELL IS COMPLETE!. Shortly after that, a haze appears over your screen, freezing the player.

You cannot move, eat or teleport until the time stop ends. The Queen Black Dragon will use all attacks at her disposal during that time, and when the ability ends the player will take all the damage in one tick.

The goal of this achievement is to survive this attack and tank all damage.

## Strategy

• Quickly complete phase 1, and ensure that a tortured soul spawns in phase 2 or 3.
• Leave one tortured soul alive during phase 2 and 3.
• Ensure the boss has some health in phase 4, or the combat will end and the "time stop" attack will not execute.
• Heal to full; lower-leveled players may want to use Immortality.
• Stand on the sides of the arena and use Protect/Deflect Ranged.
• Wait for the boss to execute the "time stop" attack.
• Kill the boss and use the last dragonkin artefact to end the encounter.

## Sources of damage

If you are standing on the edges of the arena, this leaves very few sources of damage:

• Queen Black Dragon fire walls (each wall is 1,500 damage spread in two intervals of 750 with full protection)
• Queen Black Dragon extreme dragonbreath (standing to the sides will deal 2,250 damage in three intervals of 750 with full protection)
• Queen Black Dragon auto-attacks (2,480 max without prayer)
• The tortured soul which initiated the mechanic (negligible damage)
• Any giant worms left over from previous phases/phase was ended as mechanic was active (moderate damage)

infobox.Description: Defeat the Queen Black Dragon after surviving a full time stop special attack.

achievements.description: Defeat Zemouregal & Vorkath in hard mode without using the ballista.
achievements.wikiSummary: Don't Go Ballistic is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Zemouregal & Vorkath in hard mode without using the ballista.
achievements.wikiText:
Don't Go Ballistic is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Zemouregal & Vorkath in hard mode without using the ballista.

## Strategy

Without using the ballista, players will need to manually kill off the special zombies (skeletal shielder, ghost healers and empowering zombies) themselves. They do not have a lot of health, but leaving them alive will make the kill even more tedious. The combat zombies can be dealt with appropiately by placing them southwest of the player's position and combining Threads of Fate with Soul Sap and Volley of Souls when three or more are present. This will require some luring in order to ensure the threads hit them.

The player will also be exposed to the Ice Barrage attack, which will instantly kill the player (as it deals extremely high damage if not mitigated in any way); methods to block the attack include Barricade, Protect/Deflect Magic with Devotion, or Immortality. This attack will also kill familiars if they have less than 16,000 health. The player should have enough damage to ensure that the attack is only used once, as Zemouregal begins using more damaging abilities such as Finger of Death and Death Skulls.
