Missing Mandibles is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode without anyone allowing any volatile scarab akh to spawn.

## Requirements

This achievement requires all volatile scarab akh are prevented from spawning in phases 1 and 3. Any enrage can be used for this achievement, so it is recommended that players complete it at 100% enrage.

This achievement is failed if any volatile scarab spawns, the message You have failed: Missing Mandibles: a Volatile scarab spawned. is displayed if this happens.

## Strategy

The volatile scarabs can be prevented from spawning by standing near the burrow location before the spawn. Dive is very useful for quickly travelling between burrows as each time a scarab is prevented from spawning, its cooldown is reset. The base tank that Amascut is targeting cannot leave her attack range to deal with the burrows, so it is up to the other players to do so.

It is advised to divide the arena up into 4 zones, west to east, and assign each player to one of the zones so that there is not a situation where two players are attempting to clear the same burrows, which is inefficient. Shortly before the start of the spawn animation, the players should travel (without using dive) to their assigned zone, to be ready to dive onto all the burrows as fast as they can.

Alternatively, players can skip the mechanics and deal enough damage before the scarabs spawn to complete this achievement.

## Strategy

The primary concern for this achievement is satisfying the requirements of It's Coarse and Rough and Irritating, which requires Nakatra to be defeated before she can initiate the Shadowsands mechanic a second time. Nakatra will start phase 4 with 480,000 health per player and all copies of Nefthys, the Split Soul are defeated. and the phase immediately starts with the Shadowsands mechanic.

Necromancy-using players have it a bit easier as they need to deal 30,000 less damage due to Death Mark. They should apply Volley of Souls and the death guard special after all Nefthys copies are defeated, as this will deal around 60,000 damage per player if timed properly.

As Nakatra will not perform many auto-attacks during phase 4, players should opt for an ultimate damage rotation, and use Split Soul to deal as much damage as possible. They have roughly 35 seconds after the Shadowsands mechanic to deal the necessary damage to Nakatra before she initiates it again.

achievements.wikiSummary: Nex, Angel of Death (duo) is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Nex, Angel of Death in a team of 2 or fewer.
achievements.wikiText:
Nex, Angel of Death (duo) is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Nex, Angel of Death in a team of 2 or fewer.

## Strategy

With two players, damage is significantly reduced but still feasible for an experienced player.

### Phase 1

Kill reavers as soon as they appear. Ideally, one player should use Death Mark, Threads of Fate, a death guard special, Soul Sap and five stack Volley of Souls, while the other player should launch a five stack Volley of Souls to kill reavers immediately.

Bring Nex to 2,100,000 health to start the next phase.

### Phase 2

Destroy the amalgamations as soon as they appear. The base tank will need to tank at least two of the praesuls if they do not move, since they aggro based on spawn distance. If the base tank is unwilling to tank praesuls, the DPS player will need to provoke them off.

Bring Nex to 1,800,000 health to start the next phase.

### Phase 3

Kill the praesuls off. Follow the normal order of UGCF.

Whenever a smoke plinth is sent, both players should stand in its radius if the DPS player does not have enough health to tank a 14,000 damage hit. If the DPS player has the gear to survive it, they should set it off themselves without the base tank's assistance.

Whenever ice crystals fall on players, the untargeted player should destroy them as soon as they appear to prevent the trapped player from getting hit with a powerful bleed.

Bring Nex to 600,000 health to start the final phase.

### Phase 4

Kill the crystals off as normal. Both players should ideally tank the magic attacks during this phase to limit the amount of bombs deployed and maintaining constant uptime damaging the crystals. Avoid ragging many tiles, as this will severely limit the team's options in damaging the crystals without taking immense damage.

achievements.wikiText:
Nex, Angel of Death (perfect) is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Nex, Angel of Death in a team of five or fewer without anyone dying while completing the listed achievements.

Completing this achievement awards the title [Name], the Final Praesul.

These listed achievements are all part of the Combat subcategory Nex, Angel of Death and are all members-only.

## Strategy

Players should not expect to take a lot of damage during the achievement; however, even with five players, a good amount of damage needs to be done.

### Phase 1

During phase 1, players need to bring Nex down to 2,100,000 health as quickly as possible. Blood reavers are very likely to spawn unless all five players can deal 900,000 damage before she can summon them. If they do spawn, quickly kill them off before they reach Nex.

### Phase 2

During phase 2, the attacking players each tank one specific praesul mage. The base tank can easily wipe the amalgamations with Threads of Fate. Afterwards, lure each praesul to the middle. It is highly recommended that each subsequent praesul be lured a bit after the previous one, as the kill order is extremely important for the final phase; even having one mage killed off order will drastically affect Poppin' pillars.

### Phase 3

During phase 3, some mechanics can be a bit more concerning over others:

• Smoke Blades: Players targeted by the blades should stand in the respective area in the arena to avoid having the smokes spawn at all, since getting hit by one even for a tick will result in No smoking being failed.
• Unstable Smoke: All four DPS roles should stand next to the unstable smoke crystal and consume it. This will deal 3,500 damage to each player.
• Icicle Slam: This should not be a concern, as players should be far enough from each other to avoid getting clipped by the falling icicle. This has a 5×5 AoE centred on targeted players.

### Phase 4

achievements.name: Nex, Angel of Death (solo)
achievements.description: Defeat Nex, Angel of Death solo.
achievements.wikiSummary: Nex, Angel of Death (solo) is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Nex, Angel of Death solo.
achievements.wikiText:
Nex, Angel of Death (solo) is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Nex, Angel of Death solo.

## Strategy

Solo AoD is very challenging and requires plenty of knowledge in handling the mechanics alone. Necromancy has the easiest time handling the achievement, given its high survivability rate and ease of AoE damage compared to other styles.

A beast of burden, ideally a pack yak or pack mammoth is basically required for the achievement, as the player will take immense amounts of damage during phases 2 and 3. The BoB should be filled with primal feasts, super saradomin brews, Blue blubber jellyfishes and sailfish soups.

### Phase 1

Anytime blood reavers spawn, players must stand on the quadrant Nex is facing to avoid her from getting damage stacks. To kill the reavers the rotation Invoke Death, Threads of Fate, a death guard special, Soul Sap and a five stack Volley of Souls can be used. Any reaver below 10,000 health will be instantly killed by Death Mark. It is important to kill the reavers once the icicles lift, as failing to do so will result in them transferring their health to Nex, 50% of which will be dealt as damage. Basically, if Nex absorbs at least 20,000 health, the player will likely get killed if they are not under the effects of a powerburst of vitality.

Alternatively, players can lure Nex away from the reavers once the icicles lift, stacking the reavers with sticky bombs and killing them off. This is a bit slower however.

Get at least two stacks of Residual Soul before starting the next phase, which occurs at 2,100,000 health.

It is ideal to phase Nex whilst she jumps in the air to do her elements special attack, before she spawns a new set of blood reavers. This will give the most amount of time to phase the next phase before getting new reavers.

### Phase 2

If Nex was moved during the previous phase, move her back to the centre of the arena. Wait for the amalgamations to spawn and use Threads of Fate, Volley of Souls, Soul Sap and Volley of Souls to kill off the amalgamations. This will cause the four praesuls to appear shortly after their destruction with 150,000 health. Swap to Protect/Deflect Magic at this point, since tanking four praesuls will deal much more damage than Nex's auto-attacks.

When the Praesuls spawn they can be lured onto the same tile to more effectively kill them using area of effect abilities. One method is to run to any corner of the arena and wait for the Praesuls to run towards you.

Phase Nex to 1,800,000 and kill the praesuls. Use area of effect abilities such as Spectral Scythe and Command Phantom Guardian to damage all targets at the same time. If Nex was phased during the elements attack in phase 1, Threads of Fate will come off cooldown before the next elements attack occurs. It is possible to use Invoke Death and use an aoe ability to apply the effect to all targets.

The praesuls periodically stun, the easiest way to deal with this is to use Freedom for the first stun, and Anticipate when threads of fate is about to come off cooldown to avoid the second stun.

### Phase 3

Finish off the praesuls if they did not die yet in phase 2. Unlike normal AoD where the preferred rotation is UGCF, the rotation for solos swaps G and U for GUCF (kill Glacies first instead of Umbra). This is extremely important, as the ice crystal's freeze will apply faster than Freedom being available in phase 4; destroying it first will thus make it easier to heal with Soul Split and Resonance.

Once all praesuls are killed, players can go back to flicking Deflect Melee/Magic and Soul Split. Unstable smoke crystals are fairly dangerous, as leaving them alone will deal the player 37,500 damage after resetting all defensives, likely killing the player instantly. Interacting with the crystal will instead deal 14,000 damage, which is survivable by players using life points boosts like powerburst of vitality, bonfire or Totem of Vitality, thermal bath, or high-level tank armours such as Deathwarden robe armour. A hellhound will also reduce the damage by 20% despite the damage being typeless. Ice crystals are also problematic, as players will be taking moderate bleed damage due to the crystal not being destroyed on time; this damage can be reduced with spirit shields and Shield Dome.

Once Nex reaches 600,000 health, the final phase will start.

### Phase 4

As the only player in the arena, this means that the player will always be targeted by the elements. This attack will start roughly 3 auto-attacks into the phase, after which it will be continually applied until the end of the encounter.

Keep Deflect Magic on at all times while the ice crystal is active, as failing to do so will result in getting frozen, which combined with shadow traps becomes fatal. Once the crystal is dealt with, Soul Split flicking is optional.

Apply Death Mark to each crystal as they become attackable. Each crystal has 200,000 health, but Death Mark will trigger at 30,000 health, meaning only 680,000 damage is needed for the crystals.

Use Freedom whenever the ice crystal is about to entrap the player if it is active.

The first stage of the instant kill bomb triggers roughly 9 seconds after it is applied, while the second stage applies around 10 seconds. The bomb will then appear 2 seconds after the second bar fills. Another bomb attempt is applied immediately once this bar fills. A player with good damage should be able to destroy each crystal within two bomb cycles. Bombs have a 7x7 AoE from the centre tile where they were deployed, so try to avoid ragging good tiles as this will force the player to use alternate methods to reduce bomb damage. The bombs deal 3,000 soft typeless damage if caught in the blast, so using defensives like Reflect and Disruption Shield can help mitigate damage.

Once the last pillar is destroyed, return to attacking Nex. If the player is skilled enough, they can stack bombs on each other, allowing for more space to manuver around. However, this requires subsequent stacked bombs to be placed perfectly, or the damage caused from stacked bombs will deal tremendous if not outright fatal damage onto the player.

achievements.wikiText:
Nex, Angel of Death (unorthodox) is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Nex, Angel of Death in a team of 5 or fewer without anyone dying while completing the listed achievements. If a player dies, but Nex is killed before the player's death animation finishes, the achievement will still complete as long as the required achievements are met.

Completing this achievement awards the title [Name], the Angel of Death.

These listed achievements are all part of the Combat subcategory Nex, Angel of Death and are all members-only.

## Strategy

Players will be expected to take plenty of damage for this achievement. It is recommended to bring tank armour and pack yaks with strong healing items such as Saradomin brews and sailfish or higher. Necromancy provides better sustain and stronger AoE capabilities, and so should be used by the minion tanks. Cryptbloom armour with Animate Dead provides better overall protection for the base than other styles due to most damage being from magic, and dodge only affecting Nex's melee auto attacks and providing no protection against her mechanics. Cryptbloom with Animate Dead also allows the base to rely less on defensives, meaning they can continue tanking Nex (alongside her Smoke Blades) even when they reach 15 stacks without the need to swap aggression.

### Phase 1

During phase 1, players should try to bring Nex's health close to the 2.1 million cap while stacking Shattering bones and Storm Shards stacks. Shattering bones will bring hit chance to 100% easily without needing to use Statius's warhammer in the final phase.

Players should be able to bring her down to 2.6 million health when the first set of reavers spawn and then down to 2.2 million when the second set of reavers spawn easily, giving them plenty of time to build stacks. Reavers should be brought down low, around 8,000 to 10,000 health each; this will deal around 12,000 to 15,000 damage across five players. As for the shadow orbs she uses after the first set of reavers, players should stand still until all 3 have dropped down on them before moving to another tile in order to prevent unnecessary placement of them on other tiles.

When the second set of reavers spawn, reduce their health as usual and let Nex absorb them before triggering the next phase.

### Phase 2

Once the amalgamations spawn, she should quickly be brought down to 1.8 million health to bring her to phase 3 to prevent her from using her elemental lockdown mechanic again. Players should avoid using Death Skulls, as they will likely bounce onto an amalgamation and destroy it. Likewise, the base tank should avoid Threads of Fate, as they will bounce onto the amalgamations.

### Phase 3

Once the minions spawn and the 4 minion tanks have taken aggression from them, they should all stand on the same tile as base and use protect/deflect from magic. Reserve Freedom for the icicle slam, using Anticipation instead to avoid any stuns from the praesuls, who will use Impact and Asphyxiate. The So icy achievement only requires players to be not freed from the icicle, and using Freedom will help remove the bleed that applies. Players targeted by the icicle should warn other players to avoid clipping them with its AoE.

While bringing Nex down to 600,000 health, players will need to worry about three mechanics. Here is how each of them should be dealt with:

• Smoke Blades: players should use Devotion once the Smoke Blades appear. Debilitate and/or Reflect can be used if Devotion is on cooldown. If needed, the base tank and a minion tank can swap aggression, since Nex will reset her target's defensives on a melee hit if she has 15 stacks.
• Icicle Slam: the player targeted should use Freedom and run away from the group and ensure they have enough health to tank it. If Smoke Blades is active during this mechanic, the player should ensure they stay on at least one of them so they keep taking damage from it. Once the Icicle goes away on its own, the player should go back on the same tile as the team.
• Unstable Smoke: players should simply eat up and ensure they have the health to tank it when it pops. It will deal 7,500 typeless damage to each player in a team of 5.

Be wary of certain overlaps between mechanics. For instance, Nex could send out an Unstable Smoke and then follow it up with an Icicle Slam. The player will need to be ready to take the hit from the Unstable Smoke and the Icicle Slam at the same time. Powerburst of vitality can be used as an emergency. Another example is Unstable Smoke then Smoke Blades. Players should wait until Unstable Smoke pops before using defensives, as Unstable Smoke resets defensives.

### Phase 4

When Nex reaches 600,000 health, they should focus on killing Umbra, Glacies, Cruor, and Fumus, in that order while still dealing with the above mechanics. Once Fumus is the last minion alive, players should build up adrenaline and soul and necrosis stacks before moving killing him. Players also need to be wary of the timing on when Fumus is killed, since players will need to tank smoke blades if they appear. Players also need to be wary if Unstable Smoke is used upon entry to phase 4, as it can catch the team unaware with a 7,500 hit, especially if someone has taken damage from the shadow traps.

Once phase 4 has begun, the base should lure Nex away as normal while the shadow crystal is dealt with. Base can then help with the remaining pillars if needed or keep Nex away so the rest of the team can use Split Soul for extra damage. Experienced players can use Split Soul even if Nex is within range.

The first bomb is launched around 3 auto-attacks from the start of the phase; the first bar fills in roughly 9 seconds, the second in 10, and the pulse starts appearing 2 seconds after the second bar fills.

There are three ways of dealing with placing the "Mark of the Elements" bombs at the middle of the arena:

• One-tick it: as soon as the bar fills up, players will dive/surge to the centre and immediately Surge/Dive a tick after for both the first and second bar. With enough practice, players can easily place as many bombs in the middle without anyone taking any damage.
• Tank the bombs: using Debilitate on Nex, Reflect, powerburst of vitality, or Barricade can reduce the amount of damage the bombs deal. If players are not confident using the one-tick method, they can wait outside the centre, and then run inside when the bar is almost full so they don't take extra damage.
• If ticks are missed, players are recommended to keep their health to full and use Reflect or Barricade. The bomb deals 3,000 soft typeless damage for every pulse it emits, and stacks on top of other bombs which can potentially result in an instant kill if enough bombs are stacked on each other.
• Tank the instant kill: if a player that is marked simply chooses to ignore the mechanic, they can simply take the instant kill and use up their sign of life. This will result in the player losing their adrenaline and any Necromancy stacks, but they will not be required to place a bomb.

If there are players having difficulties, spells such as Heal Other and even Intercept with Barricade can be used to assist them. Although players will need to keep in mind that Barricade requires 100% adrenaline and so will result in lower damage output. Using Shatter if Storm Shards were stacked earlier can also help with finishing the fight faster, but is not necessary, even in an average team.

achievements.description: Defeat Raksha, the Shadow Colossus without letting him use his 'Shadow Bomb' attack in phase 4.
achievements.wikiSummary: No Bombs Allowed is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Raksha, the Shadow Colossus without letting him use his "Shadow Bomb" attack in phase 4.
achievements.wikiText:
No Bombs Allowed is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Raksha, the Shadow Colossus without letting him use his "Shadow Bomb" attack in phase 4.

## Strategy

During phase 4, Raksha will use Tail Sweep every two auto-attacks if the player is within two game squares of him. Otherwise, he will use a Shadow Bomb attack instead, which will fail this achievement.

As the achievement only requires players to not let Raksha launch a shadow bomb, players can simply tank the Tail Sweep attacks if they need to. When collecting shadow anima after a shadow detonation, run back to Raksha, the Shadow Colossus after running through a quarter of the arena to avoid a bomb being launched.

achievements.name: No Friendly Fire
achievements.description: Defeat Vorago without anyone being hit by damage reflected by his 'Target Link' attack.
achievements.wikiSummary: No Friendly Fire is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Vorago without anyone being hit by damage reflected by his "Target Link" attack.
achievements.wikiText:
No Friendly Fire is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Vorago without anyone being hit by damage reflected by his "Target Link" attack.

## Strategy

Vorago can use his "Target Link" attack during phases 2, 3 (except Scopulus rotation), 4, and 5 in normal mode. This mechanic causes Vorago to reflect damage dealt to him to other players in the group. In hard mode, reflects are used in phases 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11.

This achievement requires that no damage is dealt to Vorago for the duration of the reflect. The simplest way to achieve this is to use Cease to stop attacking in advance of the reflect, letting any persistent damage effect like Magma Tempest and Death Skulls time out, then waiting until Vorago starts his next special attack before resuming attacking. It is highly recommended that Crackling and Aftershock be avoided, as their random activations can occur during reflect and cause damage, failing the achievement. It is recommended to read the strategy guide for the rotation to know the appropriate times to stop and restart attacking.

By default, all players are eligible for this achievement, and it is only once any amount of damage is reflected that the message You have failed: No Friendly Fire appears and the achievement is no longer awarded. Thus completing a kill where one or more reflect mechanics are skipped, such as by ending phase 3 or 5 before reflect happens, will not invalidate the achievement.

## Achievement set

Completing this achievement in a hard mode Vorago instance is one of the requirements for the Vorago (HM) (perfect) grandmaster achievement.

achievements.name: No More Tears
achievements.description: Defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode without allowing any Engulfing shadow tears to explode.
achievements.wikiSummary: No More Tears is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode without allowing any engulfing shadow tears to explode.
achievements.wikiText:
No More Tears is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode without allowing any engulfing shadow tears to explode.

## Requirements

Engulfing shadow tears spawn in phase 6 of the Amascut fight, around the attackable Engulfing shadow. They have a timer bar above them to countdown until they explode, which heals the engulfing shadow. Clicking on them will remove them, but put a timer bar above the player which will deal magic damage when it ends. The more tears that the player clicks, the more magic damage they take.

This achievement requires that all tears are clicked by players, with none left to time out and heal the engulfing shadow. Additionally, when the fragment of Tumeken is reformed in phase 6 by the player climbing the platforms, any remaining shadow tears will explode early. Any enrage can be used for this achievement, so it is recommended that players complete it at 100% enrage, unless they are looking to complete the perfect achievement, which requires 2000% enrage.

This achievement is failed if any tear is not clicked, which will display the message You have failed No More Tears..

## Strategy

Clicking the shadow tears to prevent the engulfing shadow from healing should be done anyway during any Amascut kill, so this achievement simply requires that players do not make any mistakes while doing so. Some tips to make this easier:

• There is no range limit to clicking on tears, and multiple tears can be clicked in the same game tick.
• The damage taken from clicking on tears is a single hit of magic damage, so players should pray magic and may optionally use defensive abilities such as Resonance.
• Tears spawn in 4 waves, with each wave containing more tears, and each wave spawns as the player climbing the platforms reaches a new platform.
• If your team is struggling to click all the tears, have the climber slow down. This may require a player to stand on the hieroglyphs to extend the Collapse timer for the phase.
• The final wave of tears must be cleared before the climber reforms the fragment of Tumeken located on the final platform, or the achievement will fail due to the tears exploding early.

## Achievement Set

Completing this achievement at 2000% enrage is one of the requirements for the Amascut, the Devourer (perfect) grandmaster achievement.

achievements.wikiText:
Not a Moth is an achievement that requires the player to defeat the black stone dragon, the last boss of the Dragonkin Laboratory, without taking damage from any shadow flames.

## Strategy

This achievement can only be completed in a normal run of the dungeon; story mode will not count.

The "shadow flames" the achievement is referring to are her dragonfire spiral and flying rampage attacks. The dragonfire spiral attack is first used after the four black hands are destroyed. The flying rampage attack is used upon reaching 260,000 or lower health when she attempts to perform her next attack. Players who are worried about being hit by the flames (as they will also trail the player on their location if one was sent at them) can hide in the upper section of her arena, where only one landing spot has the potential to emit flames at the player. This is much slower, but otherwise guarantees minimal, if no flames.

One At a Time is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Kerapac, the bound in hard mode without letting him jump more than once each phase from his 'Jumping Slam' attack. This achievement does not require a solo instance; it may be completed in a group of up to 3 players.

## Strategy

Kerapac uses his jump slam attack as the second special attack of each phase. He will attempt to jump up in the air and slam down on the player with his aggression 3 times. However, if the player he is targetting does not dodge the slam then he will remain in place, rapidly pulsing melee damage in an area around him until the player leaves the range of the damage. He can be stalled in this state where he will not perform a second jump slam attack, although the melee damage increases over time. Attempting to use Devotion will cause him to automatically remove it, though it will not affect those applied from the Devoted and Enhanced Devoted perks.

In phases 2 and 3, Kerapac will summon time clones which repeat the locations that he targetted with jump slam in the previous phases. In groups, he will summon additional time clones to perform this attack on other players, however those clones do not affect the achievement. These clones for other players also get repeated in later phases.

### High damage strategy

With sufficient damage, it is possible to reduce Kerapac to 50k health to cause his phase transition before he performs the second attack of a jumping slam. This means that the slam does not need to be stalled at all, and no time clones of the slam will appear in later phases.

### Lower damage strategy

If the group does not have the damage to skip the jump slams, then one player should be designated as base to stall Kerapac's first slam. They should rotate defensive abilities such as Immortality and Barricade to survive the melee damage, while the other players bring Kerapac's health to below 50k to cause the phase to end. While the Devotion ability cannot be used, the Devoted and Enhanced Devoted perks will work and are very useful.

Remember that Kerapac will use time clones to repeat the slams from the previous phase, so a different spot should be used in each phase to stall the slam.

### Infinite stall strategy

This strategy turns the achievement from a DPS check to being fully a tanking check.

If a slam is successfully stalled for 60 seconds, Kerapac will give up on the remaining 2 slams, and will progress to his attack pattern. This can be achieved by using a combination of:

• Cryptbloom armour
• Animate Dead
• Earth or shadow spells (to improve cryptbloom's damage reduction)
• A Staff of Light special attack (must be in an Essence of Finality as it is lost if the staff is unequipped)
• The weaken debuff spell
• Powerburst of vitality to temporarily reduce incoming damage by 50%

and rotating the defensive abilities Immortality and Barricade. This strategy will still cause the player to take significant damage, so a beast of burden with high healing food or potion flasks is highly recommended.

The player will then get Kerapac's Lightning Wall special attack, before he repeats his attack cycle from Shatter. If he is not reduced to 50k health to end the phase quickly, he may perform a second Jump Slam attack. This will not invalidate the achievement, and the first slam of his second set should be infinitely stalled just as the first slam of the first set was stalled.

So long as the player can survive, it is possible to stall indefinitely in each phase, however if more than 2 full stalls are required per phase it is likely to require more healing than the player can carry.

## Achievement set

If this achievement is completed solo in the same kill as Canon Event and Pruning the Timeline, it will award the Kerapac, the bound (unorthodox) grandmaster achievement.

## Strategy

All three black crystals must be destroyed within a single minute after stunning Seiryu the first time. Considering the shadow enigmas that will attempt to heal the crystals, two of them should be destroyed before the enigmas start healing them, allowing the player to focus what time they have left on destroying the last crystal.

Dominion mines are highly recommended for this section of the fight as the crystals do not have any combat level, making them susceptible to the mines. This deals 20,000 damage for every pair placed. Up to four mines can be activated with correct timing; if off by even a few seconds, the latter two mines will be wasted.

Invoke Death is also recommended as it allows players to instantly destroy the crystals when their lifepoints are reduced to 30,000.

## Trivia

• The achievement name is a reference to the song "Cha Cha Slide" by DJ Casper.

## Strategy

Players should aim to deal as much damage as possible, as soon as the fight starts, as Astellarn will take full damage until she initiates the celestial rain. When a player is targeted for a wyrmhole, that player should run to the edges of the arena, spawn the hole there, then run back to the boss. The neutron star that shortly follows will spawn around the player(s), including tiles occupied by the wyrmhole, which would automatically fail the achievement.

A neutron star will deal around 5,000 typeless damage across the entire arena if it makes contact with a player, but players can alternatively run away from it rather than needing to tank it.

While Astellarn takes significantly reduced damage when out of phase, notably poison damage, along with those caused by Split Soul or the eldritch crossbow's special attack will still deal full damage, and thus players should maintain as much upkeep as possible on these sources. Necromancy-using players who use Death Mark will need to apply it three or four times, as it will not be able to kill her immediately when she falls below 30,000 life points.

Parkour! is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Vorago after personally jumping onto Vorago's back in phase 1 in under 35 seconds. This can be done in a public encounter.

## Strategy

Position of the base tank Path taken by the climber

This achievement is personal; it will not be awarded to other players in the group except for the player who performed the jump.

This achievement requires that the base gets Vorago into position without needing the climber to Provoke Vorago. There are a number of ways to do this, one of which is for the base tank to stand 3 tiles west of the Jump! Gap (see picture) and have Vorago east of them and up against the north wall. Then, the base tank should dive to the square directly south of Vorago such that he faces away from the Gap. This allows the climber to immediately jump onto Vorago as soon as they get to the gap.

Alternatively, if the fight is done solo, the jump can be done immediately since Vorago will be automatically on the right position without any provoking.

The climber should make use of the movement abilities (Surge, Double Surge, and Dive) to progress through the climbing path as fast as they can, as well as effects such as Mobile, Shadow's Grace, and powerburst of acceleration. See the strategy guide for a guide of where to use which ability. As soon as the climber reaches the gap they should jump, and if they were fast enough then they will see the message You are eligible for: Parkour!.

achievements.wikiSummary: This article contains information about the recently released Havenhythe continent.
achievements.wikiText:
This article contains information about the recently released Havenhythe continent.

Some information may still be missing. You can edit the article, give feedback, or join the wiki Discord to contribute any new information.

Protect from Ivar is an achievement that requires the player to use the correct prayer against all 3 of Ivar, King of Bones special attacks.

Ivar will trigger his special attacks in a random rotation. The special attacks that must be prayed against are:

If the correct prayer is used, Ivar will complain that his attack didn't work. The player must be within the blue square marking the area of the attack or it won't count towards the achievement. If one of his attacks is not correctly prayed against or is avoided, then the achievement can still be progressed by using the correct prayer on the next time Ivar uses that attack. It is not required to use the correct prayer every time he uses one of these attacks, only that each of the 3 attacks is correctly prayed against at least once, and it is all done within one kill.

After using the correct prayers, the player must defeat Ivar to complete the achievement.

If you have difficulty seeing the cues/signals, bring plenty of good food, turn off auto-retaliate, turn on the first prayer, and tank damage until you get hit with the correct special attack. After you get the message "You have made progress towards "Protect from Ivar" (1/3)", switch to the second prayer, and repeat. And then the 3rd. Once you succeed with all 3 types and see the "You are now eligible for 'Protect from Ivar'." message, turn retaliate back on and kill him.

Similarly, high-level players would likely kill him long before he can use all three types of attacks and must turn auto-retaliate off and only kill him after using prayers to block each attack.

achievements.name: Protector of the Sun God
achievements.description: Defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode without allowing Tumeken to be damaged during phase 5.
achievements.wikiSummary: Protector of the Sun God is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode without allowing Tumeken to be damaged during phase 5.
achievements.wikiText:
Protector of the Sun God is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode without allowing Tumeken to be damaged during phase 5.

## Requirements

This achievement requires that Tumeken does not take any damage in phase 5. He will only take damage from three sources:

• Amascut's green projectiles while his fragments are being charged
• Lightstealer salawa akh after he is reformed
• Amascut's green projectiles while she jumps around the center of the arena

Any enrage can be used for this achievement, so it is recommended that players complete it at 100% enrage, unless they are looking to complete the perfect achievement, which requires 2,000% enrage.

This achievement is failed if Tumeken takes any damage, which will display the message You have failed: Protector of the Sun God..

## Strategy

Blocking Amascut's green projectiles and killing the lightstealer salawa akh should be done anyway during any Amascut, the Devourer kill, so this achievement simply requires that players do not make any mistakes while doing so. Some tips to make this easier:

• The two players alternating intercepting the green projectiles should know in advance who is taking the first projectile, and be in position before she winds up to throw them. This is especially true at the start of the second (or higher) cycles.
• Dive can be saved to allow the intercepting players faster movement into position, and Prism of Salvation used for the return.
• The player wrangling the lightstealer salawa akh should make use multi-target abilities to kill as many of them as quickly as possible, to reduce the number of akh that need to be finished off once Tumeken is reformed.
• Other players can assist in killing any remaining akh before reforming Tumeken, although some akh will always spawn between reforming Tumeken and Amascut becoming attackable.

## Achievement set

Completing this achievement at 2,000% enrage is one of the requirements for the Amascut, the Devourer (perfect) grandmaster achievement.

## Strategy

The nine-second timer allows for five global cooldowns after the first echo dies, in which to kill the remaining echoes.

A reliable way to complete this achievement is to make use of Invoke Death. Each Echo of Kerapac should be lowered to around 20,000 life points without applying any bleeds or Death Mark. This may be done with any combat style. Then, the sequence to kill the echoes is to cast Invoke Death and then use any necromancy basic ability on a clone, which will kill it instantly if the attack lowers its life points below 20,000. This is then repeated for the other two clones, making use of Dive or Surge to quickly move to them.

## Achievement set

Raksha, the Shadow Colossus (unorthodox) is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Raksha, the Shadow Colossus solo while completing the listed achievements.

Completing this achievement unlocks the shadow manifestation pet and awards the title [Name], the Shadow Colossus.

These listed achievements are all part of the Combat subcategory Raksha and are all members-only.

## Strategy

Players will need to rely on prayer flicking, as Raksha's auto attacks deal significant damage at 100% shadow energy. Debilitate, Reflect, Barricade, and powerburst of vitality should be carefully cycled through for the rockfalls and Mind Flay attack. Clearing the pools on phase 3 should be considered, as Raksha will heal significantly if they are left alone, and phasing Raksha to phase 4 may be difficult due to Raksha's 25% damage reduction from 100% shadow energy and needing to save cooldowns for the final phase.

Stacking up Storm Shards in phase 1 while Raksha builds up to 100% shadow energy will also help with damage in phase 4.

### Phase 1

As described in the strategy for Scenario 7, phase 1 must be stalled for long enough such that Raksha gains 100% shadow anima. This takes a minimum of 3 minutes 23 seconds, assuming that the player Barricades inside a shadow bomb smoke and allows for 2 cycles of absorbing the shadow anima pools.

### Phase 4

The biggest hurdle for this achievement is phase 4, as the player needs to make sure Raksha only uses shadow bombs but without being stunned by it and the fight is prolonged due to Raksha's damage reduction. In phase 4 Raksha will uses a shadow bomb every 9.6 seconds, and uses 7 shadow bombs attacks between each blue dome special attack. The stuns may be avoided by using any of:

• With a Clear Headed 3 or 4 perk, it is possible to have one use of Anticipation last long enough to cover two consecutive bombs, however the ability will be on cooldown for every 3rd bomb as it has a 24.6 second cooldown.
• Freedom will prevent one stun, however it has a 30 second cooldown so it can only be used for every 4th bomb.
• Freedom lasts for 6 seconds, so it is just possible to use it 5 seconds before a bomb to prevent its stun, and then use it again 30 seconds later to prevent the stun from the bomb 3 after.
• Transfigure gives 15 second stun immunity after the effect ends, but it requires 100% adrenaline, players will lose out on 6 seconds of DPS, and it requires careful timing on when to use it. Transfigure cannot be activated with a current stun immunity active, and it has a 3 minute cooldown.

An example sequence of stun immunities which works indefinitely:

• Anticipation and Clear Headed 4 during Raksha's second auto attack of phase 4, which covers both bombs before the first blue shield.

Then in each blue shield cycle:

• Anticipation and Clear Headed 4 during Raksha's second auto attack following the blue shield, which covers bombs #1 and #2.
• Freedom during Raksha's first auto attack following bomb #2, which will just last long enough to cover bomb #3.
• Anticipation and Clear Headed 4 during Raksha's second auto attack following the bomb #3, which covers bombs #4 and #5.
• Freedom as soon as it is off cooldown, which should be just before bomb #6.
• Anticipation and Clear Headed 4 as soon as it is off cooldown, which will cover bomb #7.
• The timing of when to use Anticipate and when to use Freedom in Raksha's attack rotation differs in order to get the 7 stuns avoided. Anticipate needs to be used just before the stun comes, whereas Freedom needs to be used earlier so that the last second or two of the Freedom effect prevents the stun. This allows Freedom's cooldown to be ready for stun 6. This can be practiced on normal kills to get the timing right.

The blue shield attack may be stalled by standing behind a pillar instead of breaking the shield, to allow time for Freedom and Anticipation to come off cooldown for the next cycle. This complete cycle is not needed if the player is able to finish off Raksha earlier by dealing enough damage.

## Trivia

• This achievement was previously called "Raksha Mechanical (unorthodox)", likely a leftover from its development process.

achievements.name: Ready, Set, Go!
achievements.description: Defeat Kerapac, the bound without being hit by his 'Jumping Slam' attack.
achievements.wikiSummary: Ready, Set, Go! is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Kerapac, the bound without being hit by his "Jumping Slam" attack.
achievements.wikiText:
Ready, Set, Go! is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Kerapac, the bound without being hit by his "Jumping Slam" attack.

## Strategy

Kerapac uses his Jumping Slam attack as the second special attack of each phase. He will attempt to jump up in the air and slam down on the player with his aggression three times. In phases 2 and 3, he will summon echoes of Kerapac which repeat the locations that he targetted with the attack in the previous phases. In groups, he will summon additional echoes of Kerapac to perform this attack on other players as well.

This achievement can be completed in normal mode in a group of up to three players, in which the most effective strategy is to reduce his life points to 50,000 before he starts his first Jumping Slam attack, thereby bypassing the mechanic altogether.

If the player or group does not completely skip the attack, it can be avoided by using Surge, Escape, or Dive at the moment when Kerapac is in the air with his wings raised fully. This will time the movement ability to avoid the attack, and if done correctly will also reset the cooldown of all movement abilities. It is also possible to stack multiple slam locations, starting on the same game square that was previously targetted, using a movement ability to avoid the attack, then running back to stand on the same game square again before repeating the process. This is particularly useful if it is expected to get all three slams in all 3 phases, since the time clones repeat the previous phases' slam locations.

## Achievement set

If this achievement is completed in a solo hard mode kill alongside Shatterproof, Definitely Can't Touch This, and Working With Myself, it will award the Kerapac, the bound (perfect) grandmaster achievement.

infobox.Description: Defeat Kerapac, the bound without being hit by his 'Jumping Slam' attack.

achievements.name: Reclaiming their Anima
achievements.description: Defeat Telos, the Warden at 4000% enrage after killing all anima-golems in phases 4 and 5.
achievements.wikiSummary: Reclaiming their Anima is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Telos, the Warden at 4,000% enrage after killing all volcanic, pure and corrupt anima-golems in phases 4 and 5.
achievements.wikiText:
Reclaiming their Anima is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Telos, the Warden at 4,000% enrage after killing all volcanic, pure and corrupt anima-golems in phases 4 and 5.

Using a deathtouched dart on Telos on phase 5 after all golems have been killed will not award this achievement.

Completing this achievement unlocks the anima-golem pet.

## Strategy

At 4000% enrage, the anima-golems in phase 4 will have 88,000 health. Three sets of golems are spawned at 112,500, 75,000 and 37,500 health. If the player is confident in their damage output, they can wait for all nine golems to appear before killing them, being wary to avoid getting Telos near them to avoid hitting it with AoE abilities, though the chances should be fairly low. Necromancy is ideal for the achievement due to its simple and high AoE capability. Use sticky bombs to bind the golems, as letting them attack while trying to handle Telos' own attacks at the same time is very likely to kill the player.

At phase 5, six anima-golems will spawn at the start of every cycle, and these have 92,250 health each. As with the phase 4 anima-golems, keeping them away is mandatory, as an attack from even one of them can deal incredibly high damage. The player should ideally try to subdue Telos within the same cycle, since allowing it to restart the cycle will result in the player having to clear the new set of golems before defeating Telos.

Rewind is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful battle against Yakamaru where he consumes a Durable Jellyfish after all his images have been defeated.

## Strategies

When the last Durable Jellyfish spawns, have one player tank it all the way to the end of the mirage phase. Lure it to melee distance of Yakamaru in the centre pool when the images are dead. Doing so when Yakamaru is at 50,000 or lower life points will result in him healing fully and resetting the entire fight, which includes poison tanking and fighting the images again.

Use Saradomin brews and defensive abilities to sustain lost life points, as supplies are likely to be depleted.

achievements.name: Rock Magnet
achievements.description: Defeat Vorago without anyone avoiding any falling rocks during the 'Ceiling Collapse' stage.
achievements.wikiSummary: Rock Magnet is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Vorago without anyone avoiding any falling rocks during the 'Ceiling Collapse' attack.
achievements.wikiText:
Rock Magnet is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Vorago without anyone avoiding any falling rocks during the 'Ceiling Collapse' attack.

## Strategy

Vorago can use his Ceiling Collapse attack during phases 3 and 4 in normal mode, but only when the rotation is Ceiling Collapse. Despite the description, it is also required to interact with this mechanic when it appears in phase 4. In hard mode, the Ceiling Collapse attack occurs in phase 3, and also in phase 9 if the rotation is set to Ceiling Collapse.

This achievement requires that every time Vorago uses his Ceiling Collapse, all players take damage from it. Shadows will appear on the ground where the rocks will fall before the damage is dealt, so that players can see where to stand. The area of the damage is slightly larger than the shadows, so there is some leeway if it is in a difficult to reach position. The rock will deal 8,000 damage, split evenly across all players in its shadow. A duo will result in both players taking 4,000 damage, trio 2,600, 4-man 2,000 and 5-man 1,600 damage. It is recommended to clear the fallen debris so that movement for later rocks is not impeded.

By default all players are eligible for this achievement, and it is only once any player does not take damage from a falling rock that the message You have failed: Rock Magnet appears and the achievement is no longer awarded. Thus completing a kill where one or more Ceiling Collapse mechanics are skipped, such as by ending phase 3 before the second Ceiling Collapse happens, will not invalidate the achievement. Any uncleared fallen rock debris that falls when transitioning to the next phase, such as going from phase 3 to phase 4, will not invalidate the achievement if players are not hit by the uncleared rock debris when it is falling down at the start of the next phase.

## Achievement Set

Completing this achievement in a Hard Mode Vorago instance is one of the requirements for the Vorago (HM) (unorthodox) grandmaster achievement.

Four of these rockfalls will always target the player during the transition. The damage dealt by the rocks are considered soft typeless, so defensive abilities such as Resonance, Reflect, and Barricade will mitigate some of the damage dealt.

achievements.name: Safety Dance
achievements.description: Avoid being damaged by twenty of the Queen Black Dragon's fire waves without defeat. Can only be completed in a solo instance.
achievements.wikiSummary: Safety Dance is an achievement that requires the player to avoid 20 fire waves spawned by the Queen Black Dragon in total in one instance of the fight. Restarting the fight will restart the counter. The achievement is awarded immediately once 20 waves have been dodged. The fight does not have to be finished.
achievements.wikiText:
Safety Dance is an achievement that requires the player to avoid 20 fire waves spawned by the Queen Black Dragon in total in one instance of the fight. Restarting the fight will restart the counter. The achievement is awarded immediately once 20 waves have been dodged. The fight does not have to be finished.

If the player gets hit by any one of the sent fire waves, then the achievement will not be awarded.

Progress towards the achievement is awarded as the last fire wave of a single special attack reaches the end of the arena platform, with the game message You avoided a fire wave in phase X.

## Strategy

• Leave auto retaliate off. Make sure a super antifire potion is active, pray Deflect Ranged or Protect from Ranged. Carry an inventory full of Sailfish as this takes around 10 minutes to complete and all damage must be tanked.
• Start the fight and stay in phase 1, and stay on the southern part of the arena so that the boss won't attack with melee.
• Do not attack the boss.
• Wait for the chat message The Queen Black dragon takes a huge breath. At this point run to the square which has a hole in the wave, staying on the southern part of the arena.
• Repeat until all 20 waves are dodged.

## Difficulty analysis

The achievement can be unlocked in any phase. Dodging the waves becomes more difficult in phases 2-4, when 2 or 3 waves appear at a time. Therefore, a player may want to avoid advancing phases.

During phase one, the fire wave is the only special attack. In the later phases they may be overridden by other mechanics. The waves are easiest to avoid since a single use of Surge or Escape will work. However, it will take much longer to finish the achievement and the player may run out of food.

Completing the achievement during phases 2–3 is harder since multiple waves have to be avoided, but progress will be twice or three times as fast. In phase 2, it is possible to dodge the first wave by standing in the correct place, then using Surge or Escape to bypass the second wave. If all fire waves are perfectly dodged, the achievement will take 6–8 minutes to complete. In phase 3, it is better to use Dive to move between the correct places if they are on opposite sides of the arena. Otherwise, it is possible to simply run between the correct places. Completing the achievement during phase 3 takes around 4-5 minutes.

There is no benefit to attempting to complete the achievement during phase 4, as the Queen Black Dragon uses the same amount of fire waves at a time as during phase 3. Additionally, there are more special attacks that will be used, leading to fewer flame walls, and more damage taken.

## Trivia

• The achievement name is a reference to the 1983 song The Safety Dance by Men Without Hats.
• The achievement name is shared with a World of Warcraft achievement obtainable in a fight against Heigan the Unclean, well known for his own special attack which requires proper positioning to be avoided.
• There is a glitch where the game will register an invisible fire wave attack if the player phases the Queen Black Dragon as a fire wave is sent, which will still count as dodged despite not appearing at all.

infobox.Description: Avoid being damaged by twenty of the Queen Black Dragon's fire waves without defeat. Can only be completed in a solo instance.

achievements.name: Scabaras Would Be Proud
achievements.description: Defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode without stopping any Scarabs from spawning.
achievements.wikiSummary: Scabaras Would Be Proud is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode without stopping any from volatile scarab akh or explosive scarab akh from spawning.
achievements.wikiText:
Scabaras Would Be Proud is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode without stopping any from volatile scarab akh or explosive scarab akh from spawning.

## Requirements

In phases 1 and 3, of the Amascut fight, she will summon volatile scarab akh approximately 28 seconds into each phase. These will be prevented from spawning if any player stands within 1 tile of the burrow that appears before the scarab does. In phase 4 she continuously summons explosive scarab akh throughout the entire phase, and can summon more explosive scarabs in phase 7 if she targets the Scabaras statue. The scarabs can only spawn in locations away from the arena walls.

This achievement requires that no player ever stands within 1 tile of a burrow to prevent a scarab from spawning. Any enrage can be used for this achievement, so it is recommended that players complete it at 100% enrage, unless they are looking to complete the unorthodox achievement, which requires 2000% enrage.

This achievement is failed if any scarab is prevented from spawning by standing near its burrow in any phase, which will display the message You have failed Scabaras Would Be Proud: A scarab was prevented from spawning.. If in any phase the scarabs are not spawned because Amascut is phased before she summons them, that will not invalidate the achievement.

## Strategy

Both volatile scarabs and explosive scarabs are required to spawn for this achievement.

### Phases 1 and 3

Players should stay directly next to the arena walls when Amascut is about to spawn volatile scarabs in phase 1 and 3, ideally standing no further south than Amascut herself. This puts them in a safe location that cannot be next to any scarab burrows. When avoiding the sanctum shockwaves in phase 3, players should move east and west, not north and south. After the scarabs spawn in these phases, players can move where they like and deal with (or ignore) the scarabs in whatever way they choose.

### Phase 4

Throughout the entirety of phase 4, players should stay at the edges of the arena. This includes not travelling across the middle of the arena by using Surge or Dive. Since each side needs 5 scarabs (1 for gorilla, 1 for chainwarden, and 3 for chains), it's recommended to have a long range weapon and prioritise the northernmost scarabs in order to prevent accidentally stepping on one. Once the scarabs are thrown, players should work their way around the outer edges of the arena, going into the portal or to the south wall and around to the statues, taking care to stand directly next to the wall. Coordinate with the player staying outside to ensure that a scarab isn't crushed when leaving the portals.

Players running a fragment of Tumeken should run directly alongside the south wall without any space between them and the wall. Once a fragment has been deposited, double back around the perimeter of the wall. Take care to not step away from the wall and onto a scarab accidentally. Players should be especially careful to not step on already-spawned scarabs, as it is entirely possible that a new spawn is hidden underneath it and causes the team to fail the achievement.

### Phase 7

Any scarabs that spawn on phase 7 as a result of Amascut calling out Scabaras during her Altar Strike attack will instantly spawn without a burrow, so there is no need to worry about accidentally blocking those and failing the achievement.

## Achievement Set

Completing this achievement at 2000% enrage is one of the requirements for the Amascut, the Devourer (unorthodox) grandmaster achievement.

infobox.Description: Defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode without stopping any Scarabs from spawning.

achievements.name: Scenario 7
achievements.description: Defeat Raksha after letting him reach 100% shadow energy in the first phase. Can only be completed in a solo instance.
achievements.wikiSummary: Scenario 7 is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Raksha, the Shadow Colossus after letting him reach 100% shadow energy in the first phase. This can only be completed in a solo instance.
achievements.wikiText:
Scenario 7 is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Raksha, the Shadow Colossus after letting him reach 100% shadow energy in the first phase. This can only be completed in a solo instance.

## Strategy

Because Raksha's attacks and damage reduction increase as he empowers himself, he will obtain a 100% damage increase and a 25% damage reduction throughout the entire fight. This makes all of his attacks extremely dangerous; all of them must be prayer flicked, and all of his special attacks must be dealt with properly.

During phase 1, Raksha will absorb anima to himself whenever he performs his Shadow Blast attack, and when the Shadow Bomb or its smoke cloud hits the player. In each Shadow Blast attack are two tail sweep/charge attacks, which spawn three shadow anima pools after the attack concludes - meaning that Raksha absorbs six pools during the first cycle, and twelve in the next. This will fill 30% of the bar on the first cycle, and 60% on the second, assuming no pools were destroyed. The shadow bomb leaves behind a shadow anima cloud, which deals heavy hard typeless damage and fills the shadow energy bar by around 0.5% with every hit. Barricade can be used to avoid this damage while still filling the shadow energy, and if used as the shadow bomb falls the bar will fill 10% before barricade ends and the player must step out of the smoke.

Thus, it is possible to fill the bar in 2 cycles, so long as each Shadow Blast is allowed to heal Raksha the full amount. There are two Shadow Bombs per cycle for four in total, Barricade should be used on the first Shadow Bomb, and then again on the third if less than 10% of the bar was filled. This results in Raksha ending the second Shadow Blast with 100% shadow energy. During all Shadow Blasts, prioritise Devotion, then Debilitate and Reflect only if needed (keep in mind that each Blast is a typical magic attack, so Resonance will also provide a full heal). A perfectly timed Devotion can only block 4 of the 5 hits, and Resonance or Disruption Shield can be used on the 5th.

Raksha will heal 30k during the first Shadow Blast, and 60k during the second. It is advised to lower Raksha's health during phase 1, without letting him reach 600k as that will trigger the transition to phase 2. Ideally, Raksha will be just above 600k as he starts the second Shadow Blast, which means that only 60k damage needs to be done to progress to the next phase.

Phases 2 and 3 proceed as usual, but Raksha will deploy five orbs for the poison mind attack, and launch seven bombs for the shadow bombardment attack. The shadow anima pools must be cleared before phase 3, otherwise Raksha will heal during his Poison Mind attack, prolonging the fight.

During Phase 4, the player will need to deal 50,000 damage during the Erebus Charge special. With high-levelled gear, this should not be any trouble; the Inner Power buff combined with the Seren godbow special and enhanced abilities with the Death's Swiftness buff will easily clear it. However, if the player is unable to deal the damage required, the instant kill can be avoided by hiding behind one of the pillars. The usual strategy of staying calm and forcing Tail Sweeps rather than Shadow Bombs, in addition to prayer switching or using Resonance on auto-attacks, still applies.

## Trivia

• The name of the achievement is possibly a reference to a codeword used by the Formula 1 team McLaren and their driver Lando Norris, which is understood to mean using 100% of the engine's capacity. This interpretation is further supported by the fact that the lead developer of the boss, Mod Ryan, is a known Formula 1 enthusiast.

## Strategy

This achievement requires the player to deal 750,000 damage within 55 seconds; while the task requires Seiryu to be defeated in one minute, jumping to the manacles takes a few seconds.

Each black crystal has 150,000 health, and in order to be able to damage them, Seiryu must take at least 300,000 damage in order to be disoriented. Players must bring several combat styles for the achievement, as there simply isn't enough time to deal the required damage with a single combat style.

Using Death Mark on the crystals will kill them at 30,000 health, reducing the total damage needed to 640,000. Two dominion mines can be used to deal 20,000 damage onto a crystal, as the crystals do not have a combat level.

## Strategy

Players who are struggling with damage should phase Nex when she initiates the virus attack, as this will cause her to use Embrace Darkness as her first special during the shadow phase. A shadow trap will deal 50% of the player's maximum health as damage, but this is usually not a problem given the long gap between traps. Shatterproof is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Kerapac, the bound without letting him send a time thread tear from his "Shatter" attack.

## Strategy

If a player stands underneath Kerapac just before he slams the staff down during the Shatter attack, he will not create a time thread tear. Some abilities may be cast without forcing the player to move from underneath Kerapac, the bound, such as conjuring a spirit or activating channelled abilities. This must be completed by every player, every time Kerapac, the bound uses Shatter, in every phase.

achievements.name: Single Sigil Solutions
achievements.description: Defeat Solak, Guardian of the Grove after using only one sigil to defeat Erethdor while Solak has at least 30% life points remaining.

achievements.wikiText:
Single Sigil Solutions is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Solak, Guardian of the Grove after using only one sigil to defeat Erethdor in phase 3 while Solak has at least 30% life points remaining.

## Strategy

It is recommended to attempt this achievement as a trio or a 4-man team. Two players should enter solak's mind realm in phase 3 to defeat Erethdor while the rest of the team brings solak closer to the life point limit.

### Phase 4

In phase 4, the entire team should enter Solak's mind realm after doing damage with several abilities in the physical realm. The players would kill all manifestations that spawn, deploy combat dummies to prepare rotations, and be split into burst DPS and mind healer roles.

In a trio, it is recommended to start off with 2 burst DPS roles and 1 mind healer, with one of the burst DPS switching after several rotation cycles to assist in upkeeping the health of Solak's mind.

In a 4-man, it is recommended to have 2 of each roles, with 2 burst DPS-mind healer pairs aligning Barricade timings to one another. Intercept and Heal Other should still be used on the entire team.

The team should prioritise healing Solak's mind while under the effect of mind healers' Barricades and Intercepts, followed by maintaining the team's own health with Heal Others, also attacking any manifestations to draw their aggression.

It is recommended to have the tier 2 Malletops perk from the Anachronia Dinosaur Farm, which extends Barricade by 3.6 seconds. Mind healers should also use a tier 90 shield without the Turtling perk to maximise the duration of Barricade without extending its cooldown.

Both roles will repeat their rotation cycles until the end of the kill.

### Burst DPS

This role is recommended to use Magic, utilising abilities such as Tsunami, Instability, and Natural Instinct, to prepare a burst DPS rotation.

Once prepared, activate Barricade and exit the mind realm, doing as much damage as possible to Solak before Barricade expires. Re-enter the mind realm when Barricade's duration is down to 3 seconds to prevent damage from the manifestations' delayed attacks.

### Mind Healer

This role is recommended to use Necromancy, as the Vengeful Ghost conjure is able to heal the player while in the mind realm. Damage reduction sources such as the Hellhound familiar are also beneficial.

This role will remain in the mind realm, and consists of killing all manifestations, deploying combat dummies, and upkeeping the health of Solak's mind by combining Barricade and Intercept.

The timing for using Barricade and Intercept should align with the burst DPS' return to the mind realm, allowing maximum healing with the entire team present. This also allows for the team's life point upkeep by using Heal Other.

If extra healing is needed for Solak's mind, the mind healer should combine damage reducing abilities such as Immortality and Reflect to allow for efficient healing during Barricade's cooldown. Powerbursts of vitality can also be used for this purpose to effectively halve damage received by the player for 6 seconds.

## Strategy

This achievement is best attempted in a 4-man encounter for a balance of damage without too much health inflation.

The primary block for this achievement is phase 1, where the team must hit the phase cap before Solak can spawn volatile rootlings. If this occurs, a reset is required, since the next mechanic will not occur until 1 minute and 5 seconds of the fight, which would waste half of the achievement time.

During phase 2, each player will tackle an anima eruption before returning to Solak. Damage from the anima storm can be ignored, though players should watch their health to avoid getting combo'ed by auto-attacks and mechanics and will last for the remainder of the fight. Deal as much damage to Solak as possible and try to end the phase before he can use his binding crush. Have Solak pre-placed on the northern pad for the start of phase 3 and deal as much damage to him as possible before the pad is blighted. The two players killing Erethdor must subdue him in one cycle.

The last phase should not be a problem; prepare adrenaline off a combat dummy if necessary before finishing Solak off.

Stand Your Ground is an achievement that requires the player to defeat each of the six Legiones without moving during the entire kill.

Using deathtouched darts will not complete this achievement, nor can they be used for the I Got This achievement.

## Strategy

The achievement starts tracking as soon as the player attacks the Legiones, due to their passive damage reduction mechanic.

Although each Legio only possesses 30,000 health, this is capped at four intervals of 7,500 health, so hits cannot deal in excess as each threshold activates the Legio's special ability. Their lightning attacks are also extremely dangerous; as the player cannot move, this means each strike will always land dead-centre on the player. These strikes are very damaging, as they have 100% accuracy regardless of the player's armour rating, and deal 2,500 damage per tick when directly hit. Protection prayers only reduce the damage by 25% rather than 50%.

The use of defensive abilities—such as Debilitate, Devotion, Reflect, and Barricade—is highly recommended when attempting this achievement. Since the achievement does not start until the player attacks the Legio, the player can move directly next to them, activate Devotion, and then unload all of their damaging abilities within the ten-second time frame of Devotion (not including the Invention variants) and kill the Legio before it expires. The achievement will only be checked for completion when the Legio fully disappears, so do not move until the drops appear. Lightning strikes can also cause delayed hits which may kill the player as the Legio dies, so the player should keep their health high to avoid being killed this way.

achievements.name: Step aside, Scarab
achievements.description: Defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode without anyone taking damage from Volatile scarab akh and Explosive scarab akh.
achievements.wikiSummary: Step aside, Scarab is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode without anyone taking damage from volatile scarab akh and explosive scarab akh.
achievements.wikiText:
Step aside, Scarab is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode without anyone taking damage from volatile scarab akh and explosive scarab akh.

## Requirements

This achievement requires that no player takes any damage from an exploding volatile scarab akh or explosive scarab akh. These Akh are present in phases 1, 3, 4, and 7. Any enrage can be used for this achievement, so it is recommended that players complete it at 100% enrage, unless they are looking to complete the perfect achievement, which requires 2000% enrage.

This achievement is failed if any player is hit by a scarab explosion, even if the damage is blocked by Barricade. The message You have failed: Step aside, Scarab: <Player> was hit by a <Type> scarab akh. is displayed if any player is hit.

## Strategy

Scarabs cannot damage players if they are prevented from spawning, or if they are properly dealt with after they spawn.

### Phases 1 & 3, high DPS

Groups with sufficiently high DPS may be able to reduce Amascut to her phase health thresholds in phases 1 and 3 before she is able to summon the volatile scarabs. This does not invalidate the achievement, as no player is damaged by a scarab. To achieve this, Amascut must either reach her health threshold before the Tear them apart voice line, to prevent the start of the spawn animation, or after all of the scarabs have fully spawned, which causes all scarabs to harmlessly explode. If Amascut reaches the health threshold during the spawn animation of the volatile scarabs, they will still spawn and deal damage when they explode.

### Phases 1 & 3, lower DPS

The volatile scarabs can be prevented from spawning by standing near the burrow location before the spawn. Dive is very useful for quickly travelling between burrows as each time a scarab is prevented from spawning, its cooldown is reset. The base tank that Amascut is targetting cannot leave her attack range to deal with the burrows, so it is up to the other players to do so.

It is advised to divide the arena up into 4 zones, west to east, and assign each player to one of the zones so that there is not a situation where two players are attempting to clear the same burrows, which is inefficient. Shortly before the start of the spawn animation, the players should travel (without using dive) to their assigned zone, to be ready to dive onto all the burrows as fast as they can. If any burrow is not cleared then the spawned scarab must be killed, which first requires stunning it.

### Phase 4

In phase 4, a great number of explosive scarabs spawn, and continue to respawn during the phase. Since explosive scarabs are required to remove the shields from the gorillas, chain wardens, and chains, it is not recommended to attempt to prevent their spawn, especially since they continually respawn during phase 4.

Instead, players should only damage the 5 scarabs on each side which they intend to use to remove shields. Care should be taken with area or multi-target abilities so as not to draw aggro from any other scarabs. Necromancy players especially should avoid having a conjured zombie during this phase, as it will passively pulse damage to any scarab it walks past. If any unwanted scarabs are damaged, they should be killed and thrown at a target such as an akh, Amascut, or thrown south out of the arena entirely. Allowing a killed explosive scarab to time out will damage players, even if it is thrown into a side room, and fail the achievement.

Since the majority of the scarabs are ignored throughout the phase, they remain where they spawn and are all simultaneously killed when Amascut ends her phase 4 stun and transitions into phase 5. As with the low DPS phase 1 & 3 strategy, players should spread out into zones shortly before this, and this time they must throw all of the scarabs south out of the arena before they explode. The base tank can assist for this set of scarabs. A limitation of throwing scarabs is that they cannot be thrown on the same tick that they are picked up. Attempting to do so will cancel the pickup action, so care must be taken to not attempt to throw the scarabs too rapidly.

### Phase 7

Amascut will only summon scarabs in phase 7 if she targets the Scarabas statue. Three scarabs must be killed and thrown onto her to remove her shield, but it is recommended to kill and throw all the scarabs to prevent any of them timing out, exploding, and damaging players.

## Achievement Set

Currently credit is also given if the tortured soul is killed due to Queen Black Dragon siphoning life from them.

## Strategy

• As this fight takes more than 5 minutes, carry an inventory full of Sailfish. Carry super antifire potions too.
• Keep auto-retaliate off and finish phase 1, 2 and 3 quickly. Kill or ignore any tortured souls that appear in these phases.
• 2-4 souls appear in phase 4. You need to surge past them to lure the chaos clouds into the souls. You just need to have 1 soul die using this method.
• Complete the kill to be awarded the achievement.

achievements.name: Stop Time Stop
achievements.description: Defeat the Queen Black Dragon after cancelling the time stop attack.
achievements.wikiSummary: Stop Time Stop is an achievement that requires the player to defeat the Queen Black Dragon after cancelling the time stop attack.
achievements.wikiText:
Stop Time Stop is an achievement that requires the player to defeat the Queen Black Dragon after cancelling the time stop attack.

## Time stop attack

During phase 2 and 3, the Queen Black Dragon will manifest tortured souls as part of her special attacks.

In phase 4, if at least one tortured soul is alive, she will execute the "time stop" attack. One of the souls will shout Kill me mortal...quickly! HURRY! BEFORE THE SPELL IS COMPLETE!. Shortly after that, a haze appears over your screen, freezing the player.

You cannot move, eat or teleport until the time stop ends. The Queen Black Dragon will use all attacks at her disposal during that time, and when the ability ends the player will take all the damage in one tick.

The goal of this achievement is to interrupt this attack after it starts.

## Strategy

• Quickly complete phase 1, and ensure that a tortured soul spawns in phase 2 or 3.
• Leave one tortured soul alive during phase 2 or 3.
• Ensure the boss has some health in phase 4, or the combat will end and the "time stop" attack will not execute.
• Stall in phase 4 and stop attacking the boss.
• Kill the soul after it shouts: Time is short!, She is pouring her energy into me...hurry!, or Kill me mortal...quickly! HURRY! BEFORE THE SPELL IS COMPLETE!.
• Kill the boss and use the last dragonkin artefact to end the encounter.

infobox.Description: Defeat the Queen Black Dragon after cancelling the time stop attack.

Strength of a Raging Fire is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Masuta the Ascended in the Temple of Aminishi with at least 7 thrashing waters still remaining.

This achievement can only be completed in normal mode.

Players should keep Protect from Magic on for the remainder of the fight, as the thrashing waters have an extremely long attack range and fast firing rate, preventing players from flicking prayers to block Masuta's ranged attacks in the final phase. As they spawn anywhere in Masuta's arena during the fight, some of these waters may be unable to attack players. A maximum of 6 waters can be safely destroyed, as the minimum amount of thrashing waters he summons is 13. The maximum that can be destroyed is seven if he summons 14 waters, but this is rare.

Prayer flicking is permitted if none of the waters are within range of the player.

## Trivia

achievements.wikiSummary: Stuffed with Anima is an achievement that is completed by defeating Telos, the Warden at at least 100% enrage after allowing him to reach a full anima bar in every phase of the fight. His anima bar can be decreased after being filled; it only needs to be filled once per phase. It is recommended to fight Telos at 100% enrage to avoid taking unnecessarily high damage.
