achievements.wikiText:
Stuffed with Anima is an achievement that is completed by defeating Telos, the Warden at at least 100% enrage after allowing him to reach a full anima bar in every phase of the fight. His anima bar can be decreased after being filled; it only needs to be filled once per phase. It is recommended to fight Telos at 100% enrage to avoid taking unnecessarily high damage. It's recommended to phase Telos when his health nears the required threshold.

During phases 1 and 2, the anima bar is increased by his tendril attack and from Telos absorbing anima from the streams.

• In phase 1, he will unleash a high damage anima bomb when his bar is filled. Using Resonance will block the damage.
• In phase 2, this extends the duration of his onslaught attack. After the bar is full, you do not need to let it drain all the way down via Magic Onslaught before moving to phase 3. Deflect Magic and Devotion should block most of the damage.

During phase 3, the green indicator must move entirely to the right end of the bar. The indicator moves to the right when Anima-golems charge Telos and when he stands in the red stream. Once the indicator is to the right of the bar, Telos begins emitting shockwaves that deals massive soft typeless damage, which should be reduced via Debilitate, Reflect, or Barricade.

During phase 4, Telos gains anima from siphoning from the fonts; the bar will always fill on the second font, unless the player tanks one of the instant-kill bombs (which is not recommended). The bar will always fill upon reaching the volcanic font if the pure font is intercepted. He uses the high damage anima bomb from phase 1.

During phase 5, Telos gains anima from using auto-attacks; the streams have no effect on his anima gain. Once his bar fills, he will charge an instant kill attack two attacks after the message appears. This can be stopped by using Immortality or a charged font.

infobox.Description: Defeat Telos, the Warden at 100% or higher enrage after letting him reach a full anima bar in all 5 phases.

## Strategy

This attack will instantly kill at full charge, dealing tremendous amounts of damage. The most reliable way to clear the achievement is to have Immortality active, as this will also bypass the executed effect when pad 2 is active. In groups, Intercepting others with Immortality can help save adrenaline.

It is also possible to complete this achievement if the 'Infernal Tomb' and 'Decimate' special attacks are skipped entirely, by bursting Zamorak's health down to the next phase before he can use a special attack in phase 2. This assumes that Zamorak only has time to use one special attack in the other phases, for a more detailed description of how special attack skips work see the strategy guide.

Falador Mole Lair

v • d • e

Sunshine Through the Rain is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Commander Zilyana in hard mode while being hit by her lightning attack and standing within their own Sunshine ability. This must be completed in a solo instance. The player must be inside both the lightning attack and Sunshine during Zilyana's death animation, not merely when her life points reach zero.

To achieve this, wait for Zilyana's lightning attack in phase 2. When adrenaline reaches 100%, activate Sunshine. Commander Zilyana in hard mode can only be defeated with an ultimate ability, which includes the damage-over-time effect caused by an enemy standing within Sunshine. However, the Planted Feet perk disables this effect. Ensure that Sunshine is activated without this perk equipped. While standing in the lightning area, the player will take significant damage, so maintaining high health is essential until her death animation concludes. The achievement can still be awarded if the player dies and is sent to Death’s office immediately afterwards.

The visual effect of the "lightning" is more likely spark-like patterns scattered across the ground.

achievements.description: Defeat Vorago after he has reflected an Ultimate ability through each of his 'Target Link' attacks.
achievements.wikiSummary: Target Acquired is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Vorago after he has reflected an ultimate ability through each of his "Target Link" attacks.
achievements.wikiText:
Target Acquired is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Vorago after he has reflected an ultimate ability through each of his "Target Link" attacks.

## Strategy

Vorago can use his "Target Link" attack during phases 2, 3 (except Scopulus rotation), 4, and 5. This mechanic causes Vorago to reflect damage dealt to him to other players in the group. In hard mode, reflects are used in phases 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11.

This achievement requires that every time Vorago uses his reflect, some damage from an ultimate ability is reflected. Depending on the rotation and mode used, the exact number of reflects may vary, but as long as every time a reflect does happen, an ultimate ability is reflected, the achievement will be awarded. There are two main strategies for this achievement:

• A very low damaging ultimate ability such as Overpower with very weak weapons such as augmented flowers or an Augmented rubber chicken. These have very low stats and will deal negligible damage even if not mitigated.
• An ultimate ability with a shorter cooldown and lower adrenaline requirements such as Tsunami with Incite Fear is used. More damage will be taken, so it is required to use defensives to avoid dying from it.

By default all players are eligible for this achievement, and it is only once a reflect ends without any ultimate ability damage being reflected that the message You have failed: Target Acquired appears and the achievement is no longer awarded. Thus completing a kill where one or more reflect mechanics are skipped, such as by ending phase 3 or 5 before reflect happens, will not invalidate the achievement.

## Achievement set

Completing this achievement in a hard mode Vorago instance is one of the requirements for the Vorago (HM) (unorthodox) grandmaster achievement.

## Strategy

Har-Aken's head will pop up to the west, east or south of the arena, and tentacles will appear on all sides of the arena. Players should avoid using abilities like Chain, Greater Chain or Death Skulls as they can potentially bounce to a tentacle, damaging or even killing it.

Additional steps to take before the wave begins to avoid killing a tentacle accidentally:

• Disable auto-retaliate
• Dismiss your familiar if using a combat familiar
• If using Necromancy, unequip lantern/switch styles to dismiss conjures

Conjures and familiars can quickly kill a tentacle even if you click away and are not attacking it yourself.

If players log out during a kill, they will not be eligible for the achievement.

achievements.wikiSummary: The Dragon Did Nothing Wrong is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Zemouregal in the Zemouregal & Vorkath encounter without killing Vorkath.
achievements.wikiText:
The Dragon Did Nothing Wrong is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Zemouregal in the Zemouregal & Vorkath encounter without killing Vorkath.

## Strategy

The player should build necrosis and Residual Soul stacks and adrenaline during the first phase, along with debuffing Zemouregal so that when Vorkath flies away at 50% HP, there will be enough burst damage to defeat Zemouregal before Vorkath returns and Zemouregal regains his damage reduction. It is possible to kill Zemouregal through the damage reduction as well, so if he is low on health after Vorkath has landed, the player may continue to focus damage on Zemouregal to finish the fight and earn the achievement.

Two casts of Death Mark are required to kill Zemouregal if damage reduction is present, as the first instance will only deal 22,000 damage.

infobox.Description: Defeat Zemouregal without killing Vorkath.

achievements.name: The Dragon Really Did Nothing Wrong
achievements.wikiTitle: The Dragon Really Did Nothing Wrong
achievements.description: Defeat Zemouregal in hard mode without killing Vorkath.
achievements.wikiSummary: The Dragon Really Did Nothing Wrong is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Zemouregal in the Zemouregal & Vorkath encounter in hard mode without killing Vorkath.
achievements.wikiText:
The Dragon Really Did Nothing Wrong is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Zemouregal in the Zemouregal & Vorkath encounter in hard mode without killing Vorkath.

## Strategy

Zemouregal has 500,000 health in solo hard mode. He is immune to damage in phase 1, so players must force Vorkath to phase 2 (1,125,000 lifepoints in solo hard mode) in order for the damage immunity to be lifted to a 90% reduction. This means players must deal 5,000,000 effective damage in order to defeat him if this method is used. A pack mammoth with mammoth feast scrolls is very helpful in bringing extra supplies due to the prolonged encounter.

Additionally, players could start attacking Zemouregal on phase 3. Vorkath will initiate Ice Barrage at the start of the phase, during which the damage reduction is fully lifted until it returns. However, this in turn will also cause Zemouregal to begin using much stronger attacks such as Finger of Death and Death Skulls. Try to dump a full attack rotation on Zemouregal to deal as much damage as possible. The player will have 30 seconds before Vorkath returns. If the player does not kill Zemouregal in time, they should continue attacking him through the damage rotation until Vorkath initiates Ice Barrage again.

Two casts of Death Mark are required to kill Zemouregal if damage reduction is present, as the first instance will only deal 22,000 damage.

achievements.name: The Hedge Knight's Dilemma
achievements.description: Defeat Silverquill, the Dreadhog, solo, using only melee and without receiving any reflect damage.
achievements.wikiSummary: This article contains information about the recently released Havenhythe continent.
achievements.wikiText:
This article contains information about the recently released Havenhythe continent.

Some information may still be missing. You can edit the article, give feedback, or join the wiki Discord to contribute any new information.

The Hedge Knight's Dilemma is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Silverquill, the Dreadhog without receiving any reflect damage and only using melee. This requires a halberd-type weapon to achieve, as during the fight standing within 1 tile of Silverquill will reflect small amounts of damage regardless of style used. Silverquill will go into reflect mode at 52,800 and 26,400 life points.

The player will be disqualified from the achievement if they deal any non-melee damage, including damage from deflection curses and blood necklaces.

Using walk instead of run will prevent getting accidentally going into melee distance.

Things that can disqualify achievement and so players should avoid:

• Being within melee distance (1 tile away)
• Combat familiars
• Bleeds
• Run toggled on
• Aftershock perk
• Crackling perk
• Deflect curses
• Area of effect abilities when hitting the blobs
• Armour spikes
• Deathtouch bracelet
• God books
• Abilities that hit more than 1 time (Assault, Hurricane, etc.)

## Trivia

• The name of the achievement is a reference to the Hedgehog's dilemma, where hedgehogs attempting to move closer to share heat in cold weather but remaining apart so as to not hurt each other with their spines is used as a metaphor to describe humans being unable to be intimate with one another without leaving themselves vulnerable to harm.
• The name may also be a reference to the television series A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, which first aired shortly before the release of this achievement and follows a protagonist who is a hedge knight.

infobox.Description: Defeat Silverquill, the Dreadhog, solo, using only melee and without receiving any reflect damage.

achievements.name: The One That Speaks But Doesn't Stun
achievements.wikiTitle: The One That Speaks But Doesn't Stun
achievements.description: Defeat Raksha, the Shadow Colossus without being stunned by his 'Tail Sweep', 'Trampling Charge' and 'Shadow bomb' attacks.
achievements.wikiSummary: The One That Speaks But Doesn't Stun is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Raksha, the Shadow Colossus without being stunned by his 'Tail Sweep', 'Trampling Charge' and 'Shadow bomb' attacks.
achievements.wikiText:
The One That Speaks But Doesn't Stun is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Raksha, the Shadow Colossus without being stunned by his 'Tail Sweep', 'Trampling Charge' and 'Shadow bomb' attacks.

## Strategy

A player with strong damage should be able to clear phase 1 before a Shadow Bomb is launched. Tail Sweep/Trampling Charge can be easily avoided by running away from Raksha when he initiates the mechanic. Players who are worried they may be unable to avoid the mechanic can activate Freedom or Anticipation in advance.

Likewise, a player with strong damage output in phase 3 should be able to clear it before Raksha can use the shadow bomb attack.

In phase 4, the sweep and bomb attacks are used every two auto-attacks. Players should stand two tiles from Raksha and then run away when he initiates Tail Sweep, which will prevent the need to use Freedom or Anticipation.

Getting hit by any of these mechanics without stun immunity will fail the achievement.

achievements.wikiSummary: The Ultimate Tank Test is an achievement that requires the player to complete a Kerapac, the bound encounter in hard mode without ever jumping into a player echo's time thread.
achievements.wikiText:
The Ultimate Tank Test is an achievement that requires the player to complete a Kerapac, the bound encounter in hard mode without ever jumping into a player echo's time thread.

This restriction means that the echoes of Kerapac will have a damage reduction as the player(s) have not entered the respective player clones, as well as all of them will be attacking the player(s) at the same time, while having 75 fury stacks applied to each echo as well as Kerapac himself. As each echo is defeated, the others will gain 50 further stacks, meaning that when Kerapac becomes damageable once more he will be at the maximum of 400 fury stacks.

This achievement may be completed with multiple players, as long as no player clones are interacted with. This makes the achievement significantly easier, as a player can focus on one or two echoes and then deplete Kerapac's life points much faster.

It is strongly recommended to use a shield for most or all of the fourth phase of the fight if attempting this achievement, as well as utilising the extra action button's Time Warp as often as players can, in conjunction with defensive abilities, such as using it to revert to shortly before casting Barricade so it may be used again once it wears off. Magic tank armour in conjunction with Animate Dead is also suggested due to the sheer length and amount of damage during the achievement attempt.

achievements.name: There Cannot Be Light Without Shadows
achievements.wikiTitle: There Cannot Be Light Without Shadows
achievements.description: Defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 1000% or higher enrage without damaging the Engulfing Shadow during phase 6.
achievements.wikiSummary: There Cannot Be Light Without Shadows is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 1,000% or higher enrage without damaging the engulfing shadow during phase 6.
achievements.wikiText:
There Cannot Be Light Without Shadows is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 1,000% or higher enrage without damaging the engulfing shadow during phase 6.

## Requirements

The Engulfing shadow spawns in phase 6 of the Amascut fight, and constantly heals itself over time. It also heals when engulfing shadow tears are allowed to time out. The higher its health is, the more black bar shield health is gained by Amascut during phase 6. This black bar shield must later be removed by damage or else the players will take damage according to how much health the shield has remaining when phase 6 ends.

This achievement requires that no damage is done to the engulfing shadow throughout phase 6. It also requires that the enrage of the fight is at least 1000%, although completing it at 2000% is one of the requirements for the unorthodox achievement.

This achievement is failed if any damage is done to the shadow, which will display the message You have failed There Cannot Be Light Without Shadows..

## Strategy

Since the shadow is left to remain at high health for the whole time it is present, Amascut will gain a large amount of health on her black bar shield, potentially over 1,000,000. There are two strategies to deal with this.

### Immortality

Teams with low damage may choose to not even attempt to clear the black bar shield, and instead survive the subsequent damage by using Immortality. For this strategy, the engulfing shadow and all shadow tears are ignored in the first part of phase 6. Once Tumeken is reformed and the Shadow of Amascut clones spawn, the players should kill them in any way that they choose. After the clones are dead, the players may build adrenaline by attacking Amascut to use immortality. The timer bar above Amascut for her stun duration lasts 25 seconds, and Immortality lasts for 30 seconds, so using immortality at any time when the bar is visible will allow it to save the players from the damage when the bar ends. Players can then build back to full adrenaline to prepare for phase 7. In encounters below 2000% enrage, Intercept may be used by one player to take all the damage, so that only that one player needs to use Immortality.

Since this strategy doesn't allow players to do any damage to Amascut herself in phase 6, it means that the team will have more health to deal with in phase 7.

### High Damage

Teams with high damage may choose to power through the high health of the black bar shield, so that they can do some damage in phase 6 to make phase 7 quicker. Some tips to help with this strategy:

• While players cannot damage the shadow, they can click the tears to slow down the rate at which the shadow heals.
• The black bar shield will have less time to grow if the player climbing the platform does as fast as they can.
• Amascut's shield takes damage before the 25 second stun caused by killing all of her clones, so the team can get more time to damage the shield if they do not kill all of the clones right away. This comes at the tradeoff that Amascut will be attacking during that time. The player who climbed will have Amascut's aggro so should be able to deal with it, and not stand next to the other players.

If successful, the team will be able to remove the black bar shield and do damage to Amascut's health bar itself during phase 6, which makes phase 7 faster.

## Achievement Set

Completing this achievement at 2000% enrage is one of the requirements for the Amascut, the Devourer (unorthodox) grandmaster achievement.

infobox.Description: Defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 1000% or higher enrage without damaging the Engulfing Shadow during phase 6.

There's Always Something Behind the Waterfall is an achievement that requires the player to participate in a successful encounter against Vorago after mitigating all damage from his "Waterfall" attacks.

## Strategy

Vorago can use his "Waterfall" attack during phase 4 in normal mode, or phase 9 in hard mode. He will always start these phases by placing a protective waterfall in one of the four corners of the arena. Players have approximately 10 seconds (reduced in hard mode) to get to the waterfall and stand behind it to avoid taking damage.

This achievement requires that for every waterfall, all players successfully stand behind it. If the kill takes longer than the minimum three waterfalls, then each additional waterfall must be used as well.

By default all players are eligible for this achievement, and it is only once any player gets hit by not standing behind a waterfall that the message You have failed: There's Always Something Behind the Waterfall appears and the achievement is no longer awarded.

## Achievement set

Completing this achievement in a hard mode Vorago instance is one of the requirements for the Vorago (HM) (perfect) grandmaster achievement.

achievements.name: They All Fell Down
achievements.description: Defeat the Dagannoth Kings solo, all within 5 seconds of each other.
achievements.wikiSummary: They All Fell Down is an achievement that requires the player to defeat all three Dagannoth Kings within 5 seconds of one another.
achievements.wikiText:
They All Fell Down is an achievement that requires the player to defeat all three Dagannoth Kings within 5 seconds of one another.

Players can only obtain this achievement in a solo private instance. Non-instanced attempts will not count towards this achievement.

As Dagannoth Kings are completely immune to necromancy damage, Death Mark cannot trigger and it is not possible to complete this achievement using Necromancy.

Extinction Event is a similar achievement that requires defeating the Rex Matriarchs.

## Strategy

• Attack the kings using your style-specific weapon and bring them each down to under 3,000 health points.
• Stand in the center of the arena, and wait a few seconds for all the kings to clump up close to each other. This reduces the running distance to execute the fatal blow.
• Stop attacking them.
• Quickly swap to each weapon and execute the fatal blow to each king. Since they are nearby there should be no distance to run/surge. It may be helpful to use a bleed or other DOT effect for the first killing blow so that it is slightly delayed.
• Dagannoth Supreme - weak to Melee weapons.
• Dagannoth Rex - weak to Magic weapons.
• Dagannoth Prime - weak to Ranged weapons.

## Equipment recommendations

Gear

• Carry one weapon (set) per style
• Since you are using low-tier armour and get hit a lot, it is best to carry brews.
• A nexus can be carried to execute defensives (optional)
• Deflect Curses and Dreadnips can be used to complete this achievement.

Setup

• Full manual combat mode helps execute abilities which do not bleed, do not do too much damage, and gain full control over the fight.
• Place each weapon into an action bar slot, keybinding each slot.

Cautions

• Avoid using Cinderbane gloves and Weapon poison++ to avoid messing up the timing.
• Avoid using bleeds and damage over time abilities.
• Style-specific armour takes too much time to swap, therefore hybrid armour is best.

## Trivia

• The achievement title is a reference to the nursery rhyme Ring a Ring o' Roses.
• This achievement could previously be obtained when fighting the Dagannoth Kings in a group, however this was changed in a patch on 6 November 2017.

## Strategy

Cleanse via Merethiel before heading up to the Anima storm so that each click will do more damage. It will usually take 2–3 pillars to completely clear the storm, but since it will slowly dissipate over time it is also possible to only go up once and then let the storm burn itself out throughout the rest of the fight.

This achievement may not pop despite the storm dissipating if the storm is killed by poison damage or time. It is more reliable to ensure that the players siphon the last bit of the storm rather than let it die off over time.

achievements.wikiText:
This Is Not True Power is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Rasial, the First Necromancer without being hit by his 'Volley of Souls' attack. Since Rasial cannot miss, and blocking the damage still fails the achievement, the requirement is therefore to prevent Rasial from ever using his Volley of Souls attack.

## Strategy

Rasial will use Volley of Souls once he reaches 5 Residual Soul stacks. He will gain this at set intervals during the fight, and whenever the two soul obelisks fully charge.

If the obelisks are not dealt with, Rasial will unleash the attack at the 1:05 mark (assuming he was only stunned once from the death guard special). Players who are unable to force Rasial to 200,000 health (to trigger phase 4's start) should deal with both obelisks when they appear to ensure Rasial will not be able to reach the five stacks needed. Additionally, using Soul Strike as frequently as possible to stun Rasial will also stall out some of his attacks that naturally accumulate Residual Soul stacks.

achievements.name: This Might Be a Catastrophe
achievements.description: Defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode after allowing her to enter phase 7 with 75% of her lifepoints remaining.
achievements.wikiSummary: This Might Be a Catastrophe is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode after allowing her to enter phase 7 with 75% of her life points remaining.
achievements.wikiText:
This Might Be a Catastrophe is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer in enrage mode after allowing her to enter phase 7 with 75% of her life points remaining.

## Requirements

Amascut's phases are not tied to her health, but rather to her attack rotation and mechanics. Each phase up to phase 6 has a method to reach its end without dealing any damage to Amascut.

This achievement requires that when Amascut ends phase 6 to transition into phase 7, she has at least 75% of her starting health. Any enrage can be used for this achievement, so it is recommended that players complete it at 100% enrage, unless they are looking to complete the unorthodox achievement, which requires 2000% enrage.

This achievement is not awarded by default, but when entering phase 7 with above 75% health the message You are now eligible for: This Might Be a Catastrophe. will be displayed if the team is eligible.

## Strategy

Since the players are limited in the amount of damage they can do to Amascut. It is advised to bring tier 1 off-style weapon with which to hit Amascut without doing damage, so that adrenaline can still be gained. Also since there are large sections without being able to deal damage, Soul Split cannot be used for healing during those times, and more food may be required. Each phase can be ended without doing damage to Amascut.

### Phase 1

Phase 1 ends when Amascut reaches the end of her attack rotation, after 1 minute 25 seconds. Only the base tank needs to be close enough to Amascut to be damaged by her, so other players should stand far away and deal with mechanics that may hurt the base, such as clearing the scarabs or diving onto the base for the "Bend the Knee" attack. The base may use weapons that aren't tier 1, if they wish to try and gain some healing from Soul Split.

### Phase 2

Phase 2 is dealt with as normal, up until Amascut is stunned by depositing the fragments of Tumeken into the statues. Players should not do any damage to Amascut at this time, returning to their positions from phase 1, optionally building adrenaline on the various minions. Phase 2 will end when both fragments are deposited and the 25 second stun resulting from that has ended.

### Phase 3

A repeat of phase 1, phase 3 ends 1 minute 25 seconds after it starts.

### Phase 4

Phase 4 is dealt with as normal, and then a repeat of phase 2 once Amascut is stunned. Phase 4 will end when both fragments are deposited and the 25 second stun resulting from that has ended.

### Phase 5

Phase 5 is dealt with as normal, until Tumeken is reformed. When Amascut is damageable and jumping around the arena, the team may consider doing some damage to her in order to bring her to around 80% of her starting health, so that she doesn't have her full health bar in phase 7.

### Phase 6

Phase 6 is dealt with as normal, until the clones have died and Amascut is stunned. The team will want to remove her black shield health bar, but then stop doing damage, and carefully and bring her health to as close to 75% as they can without overshooting. If her health dips under 75%, it is possible to heal her back by using a Calorie bomb.

### Phase 7

If at this point the team has the eligibility message, then they can complete the remainder of phase 7 in any way they choose. The high starting health means that it will likely take many cycles of her attack rotation to finish the fight, and so consistency is more important than speed. The first priority is to deal with the mechanics and movement correctly, to minimise damage taken. Only after that is damage a consideration.

• Always provoke Amascut toward the correct statue, and leave that quadrant to avoid taking damage
• Deal with crocodiles and scarabs immediately after they spawn
• Make frequent use of Dive to avoid all of her shockwaves and hieroglyphs
• Use defensive abilities such as Devotion, Debilitate, or Reflect to minimise damage taken from her triple-hit attacks

## Achievement Set

Completing this achievement at 2000% enrage is one of the requirements for the Amascut, the Devourer (unorthodox) grandmaster achievement.

Thrashing Around is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Helwyr in a solo encounter without being hit by his Thrash attack.

Thrash is his third special ability. He will leap onto the player and begin casting thrash the moment he lands. Cast a movement ability as he is leaping to avoid being clipped by this attack. Barricade does not work for this achievement despite taking no damage from the attack, as the goal is to not get hit in the first place.

The Escape ability is best used for achieving this end, as it moves the player away from Helwyr in the shortest amount of time.

Be sure to start the fight standing in the middle of the arena, then, after he has used his 'Rend' ability and 2 basic attacks, activate escape while having space around you to escape towards.

## Strategy

Wave 16 spawns three TzekHaar-Jads, however their attack rotation is staggered so that their attacks can be flicked. A total of 300,000 damage is required to kill the Jads off. Do not stun the first two Jads being killed, or they will likely attack on sync with another Jad.

To be able to reach the Jads, a weapon with attack range 7 or higher must be used. This means that melee and necromancy cannot be used for this achievement. A switch weapon can be brought for this wave if the player is not comfortable doing the entire fight with ranged or magic.

If Zuk sends a lava wall at the player while clearing the Jads, use Barricade or Immortality. A player with best-in-slot gear and high damage output should be able to kill the three Jads before the fire wall arrives.

achievements.name: To Bleed Or Not To Bleed
achievements.wikiTitle: To Bleed Or Not To Bleed
achievements.description: Defeat Vorago without anyone being hit by his 'Destroy Tank' attack in stages 2, 4, and 5.
achievements.wikiSummary: To Bleed Or Not To Bleed is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Vorago without anyone being hit by his 'Destroy Tank' attack in phases 2, 4, and 5.
achievements.wikiText:
To Bleed Or Not To Bleed is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Vorago without anyone being hit by his 'Destroy Tank' attack in phases 2, 4, and 5.

## Strategy

Bleeds are applied during phases 2 and 5 on all rotations. It will also be applied during phase 3 if the current rotation is Vitalis, and phase 4 for every rotation except The End (purple bombs). Despite the description stating stages 2, 4, and 5, it is required to deal with the bleeds appropriately during any phase in which they appear. In Hard mode, bleeds can appear in phases 2, 5, 9 (except during The End rotation), 10 (only during The End rotation), or 11 (only during Vitalis rotation).

During the bleed sequence, Vorago will apply five instances of the bleed to his target. This achievement requires that the 'Destroy Tank' debuff (bleed) is cleared before it applies damage, every time the bleed attack happens. This can be done by using Freedom or moving quickly away from Vorago with Surge, Dive, or Escape. This must be done within 1 tick of the bleed being applied. In phases 2, 3 (Vitalis) and 4 the player can avoid the bleed by running far enough from Vorago, while in phase 5, it is based on the player's location at the time of application rather than proximity to Vorago.

By default all players are eligible for this achievement, and it is only once a bleed causes damage to a player that the message You have failed: To Bleed Or Not To Bleed appears and the achievement is no longer awarded. Thus completing a kill where one or more sets of bleeds are skipped, such as by Ceiling Collapse phase 4 bleed skips or ending phase 5 before bleeds happen, will not invalidate the achievement.

## Strategy

Vorago can only summon his Scopulus minions during phase 3 in normal mode when the rotation is Scopulus. In hard mode it is phase 4 for all rotations.

The Scopulus minions can only attack with melee, so this achievement simply requires that the players constantly move, kiting the Scopulus and killing them without letting them get within melee distance. Players should be careful of them changing their target and moving unpredictably.

By default all players are eligible for this achievement, and it is only once any player takes damage from a Scopulus that the message You have failed: To Me, To You appears and the achievement is no longer awarded.

achievements.wikiSummary: Twin Furies (HM) Competent Speed Killer is an achievement that requires the player to defeat the Twin Furies in a hard mode, solo encounter in less than 1 minute.
achievements.wikiText:
Twin Furies (HM) Competent Speed Killer is an achievement that requires the player to defeat the Twin Furies in a hard mode, solo encounter in less than 1 minute.

## Strategy

The key is using Threads of Fate to damage both sisters at once, which doubles your DPS while it is active, because each sister can be damaged independently but drains health from the same health pool.

This works with Necromancy:

• Start the fight with 100% adrenaline using Persistent Rage/Infernal Puzzle Box.
• Use Living Death at the start, use an adrenaline potion and Death Skulls while running around and avoiding Avaryss who is surging across the arena. Build adrenaline and use Death Skulls again. Reserve all your high DPS abilities for later.
• When Nymora leaps into the air, run beneath her to be protected. Keep DPSing Avaryss who will follow you.
• When Nymora lands, make sure both sisters are close to you, and then perform the following DPS rotation: (this will not work if Nymora is flying)
• Split Soul
• Threads of Fate
• Volley of Souls (5-stack)
• Death guard spec/Omni guard spec
• Finish them off with Finger of Death or any other ability

TzKal-Zuk (HM) Grandmaster Speed Killer is an achievement that requires the player to defeat TzKal-Zuk in hard mode in less than 13 minutes and 30 seconds.

## Strategy

The player must defeat both Zuk and the seventeen waves in a very short amount of time.

Melee and ranged are recommended for the fastest times. Darkness and Zemouregal's nexus are recommended to increase dodge chance and access to defensive abilities, as players will not be utilising any safespots.

It is possible to reach 13:22 with only magic, Darkness, and a Hellhound (familiar), and many attempts (and otherwise full-offensive tactics) using Greater chain and the Soulfire special ability.

The player should reach Zuk within 9-10 minutes, allowing for the rest of the time to fight him and the Conduit of Ful. Zuk will force an Igneous Rain mechanic should the player somehow deal 800,000 damage in one attack cycle, which will take around 40 seconds to finish.

During the Conduit of Ful, dodge any fireballs but try to avoid having more than two launched when using melee. Even when accounting for the 50% damage reduction during superheating sequences, melee can still break it without difficulty. Make sure to tank the incoming bomb hits from Zuk with Resonance/Disruption Shield, powerburst of vitality and ring of death.

Ultra Instinct is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Raksha, the Shadow Colossus without letting him gain any shadow energy. This can only be completed in a solo instance.

## Strategy

In phases 1 and 2, Raksha will only absorb shadow anima pools upon performing his shadow burst attack. In phase 3 however, he will begin absorbing them just slightly after summoning the shadow apparition, so it is important to deal with them during the few seconds before the phase transition animation ends.

A quick method to clear all of the pools as a solo player in phase 3 is to bring a halberd-type weapon such as a dragon rider lance, Laniakea's spear or noxious scythe with laceration boots and Bladed Dive. The pools have low health and defence that Bladed Dive should kill them in one hit, and the player should repeat this for the remaining three sets of pools. It is important to ensure that the pool is clicked on and not an empty tile, or the ability will be wasted.

## Trivia

achievements.wikiSummary: Unpr-edict-able is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Zamorak, Lord of Chaos at 750% or higher enrage after activating the edicts in order of: 3, 5, 6, 1, 4, 2 (H, V, E2, B, A, E1).
achievements.wikiText:
Unpr-edict-able is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Zamorak, Lord of Chaos at 750% or higher enrage after activating the edicts in order of: 3, 5, 6, 1, 4, 2 (H, V, E2, B, A, E1).

## Strategy

The game considers the pad order from right to left, and as such each pad has their own effects when triggered:

• Pad 1 (Twinshot) - Zamorak's auto-attacks now hit twice, with the second hit being 10% of the original damage per stack.
• Pad 2 (Smite) - If a player target is below 5% of their Constitution level x 100 per stack, Zamorak's attacks will soft instant kill them.
• Pad 3 (Coven) - A lifeweaver and protector will spawn to the east and west respectively. If the player is within minimap range of them, they will move in to support Zamorak. They will spawn periodically throughout the fight.
• Pad 4 (Disintegrate) - Zamorak's attacks ignore 7% of shielding abilities (such as Reflect and Debilitate)
• Pad 5 (Chaos Traps) - Each time the next phase starts, chaos traps are placed around the arena and on all pads.
• Pad 6 (Affliction) - When Zamorak's targets heal, their healing is reduced by 10% per stack.

A stack is when a pad active and the next phase is triggered. For example, if phase 2 was started with pad 1 active, pad 1 would be given an additional stack for 20% damage.

When phase 7 starts, the order that was achieved in phases 1-6 are reversed. With the required order being 3, 5, 6, 1, 4 and 2, phase 7 would have the following effects:

• Pad 2 (Smite) - Player targets will be executed below 30% of their Constitution level x 100.
• Pad 4 (Disintegrate) - Zamorak's attacks ignore 35% of shielding abilities.
• Pad 1 (Twinshot) - The secondary hit from Zamorak's auto-attacks deals 40% of the original damage.
• Pad 6 (Affliction) - Player healing is reduced by 30%.

Zamorak will have a total of 862,500 health for phases 1-6, a starting shield value of 150,000 during phase transitions and 208,333 health in phase 7.

## Achievement Set

Completing this achievement in the same kill as the following other achievements is one of the requirements for the Zamorak, Lord of Chaos (unorthodox) grandmaster achievement.

• You're coming home with me
• Stunlocked
• I said E, not E!
• Welcome to Gielinor, it's cooler here
• You. Shall. Not. Shield.
• Unpr-edict-able

achievements.wikiText:
Unworthy Dead is an achievement that requires the player to kill 15 Summoned skeletons within 6 seconds during the encounter with Taraket the Necromancer inside The Shadow Reef.

This achievement can be completed in story mode as well as in normal mode, either in a group or a solo encounter while the fight is still ongoing (no need to kill Taraket).

Both the rift of undeath and corpse carrier summon skeletons throughout the fight while they are active, with both of them summoning three skeletons at a time around them. Try to bunch the skeletons together before using AoE abilities to quickly dispose of them, as they only have 2,000 health (1,000 in story mode). Make sure to do this before Taraket kills them to recover lost health.

Vorago (HM) (duo) is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Vorago in hard mode in a team of two or fewer.

## Strategy

In hard mode, Vorago's magic attacks will now target two players at a time; this achievement essentially means they will be both taking magic attacks, and the base tank will also have to handle the periodic melee swipes in the phases Vorago chases after them.

Use of Intercept and Barricade are essentially required, since they will help reduce a lot of damage in several phases, especially phases 10 and 11.

It is best to attempt the achievement with the primary rotation being TeamSplit, as it has the least dangerous mechanics for phases 10 and 11; two instances of TeamSplit for phase 10, and one instance of both it and purple bombs on phase 11. The other primary rotations spawn Vitalis on phases 10 and/or 11, which contribute to pushback and can be very tedious to handle while dealing with Vorago at the same time.

## Strategy

In a trio, the third player becomes a bomb tank since Vorago launches two magic attacks in hard mode rather than one, and this targets the players furthest from him.

The achievement can be attempted on any rotation as the presence of a third player makes the rotations on phase 10/11 much less dangerous. Using Intercept and Barricade will help prevent a lot of damage, especially in phases 10 and 11.

## Strategy

Additional food is required for this achievement, as players will be taking unnecessary amounts of damage while completing it, especially from achievements Lets Stay Together and Dry as a Bone. Target Acquired can be completed by using a weak main-hand weapon of a style not being used, resulting in minimal damage. Rock Magnet is less of an issue as it only occurs in phase 3, but players attempting the achievement with Ceiling Collapse will also have to handle it on phase 9.

Completing the achievement Comeback kid requires that players be on the last possible set of rows on both phases 10 and 11, making timing absolutely crucial to avoid losing the attempt.

achievements.name: Vorago (solo)
achievements.description: Defeat Vorago solo.
achievements.wikiSummary: Vorago (solo) is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Vorago solo.
achievements.wikiText:
Vorago (solo) is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Vorago solo.

## Strategies

Solo Vorago requires immense experience; while he only has 250,000 health per phase, many of Vorago's phases are timegated by mechanics, making the attempt a test of endurance.

It is best to attempt a solo with the Team Split rotation, as it is the least dangerous of the special attacks. Ceiling Collapse is another alternative but can potentially result in more damage with poor damage output.

Due to the player needing to tank 5 hits of Destroy Tank (or 3 in phase 5) in the phases that he uses them, players are essentially required to have the Mobile perk (or Shadow's Grace relic), Dive, Double Escape or Surge, and Freedom. Double Escape and Surge provide two free cancels, Freedom provides a third, Dive provides a fourth and the cooldown from Mobile or Shadow's Grace will reset Escape or Surge by the time Vorago comes for the fifth smash. Numbing roots can also be used to clear one of the bleeds. Alternatively, the player could run away from Vorago between smashes, but this is only the case if the player doesn't have a reduced cooldown.

In phase 5, the player must know how to deal damage while avoiding damage at the same time due to the pushback mechanic. It is essentially required to have Disruption Shield, and prolonging Barricade is just as important since these are the only two ways to consistently prevent pushback from Vorago.

Vorago Grandmaster Speed Killer is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Vorago in a team of 2 or fewer in less than 6 minutes and 30 seconds.

## Strategy

This achievement is only possible on the "Ceiling Collapse" rotation. Achieving a Grandmaster kill time allows for an extremely minimal amount of leniency even when using perfectly optimised strategies, including:

• Climbing with a powerburst of acceleration
• Solo luring
• Ending phases 1, 2, and 4, the tick Vorago becomes attackable again
• Centring Vorago on phase 2 and not moving him during bleeds
• Activating the gravity field as quickly as possible
• Performing a clone skip on phase 4 by walking Vorago out of attack range of the other player
• Performing a bleed skip on phase 4 by safespotting Vorago with a boulder and using Cease to prevent him from applying more than 1 bleed.
• Utilising target cycling on phase 5 to perform a "0-Spec" and push Vorago to maul spot before he uses the Teamsplit special attack.

It is recommended for both players to use melee. Melee's high burst damage compliments the shorter damage phases followed by long time gated phases allowing time for Berserk to come off cooldown again. Using the dragon scimitar special attack in the fight's down time lets players reach 100% accuracy using slash weapons without the need for accuracy improving debuffs or a nihil.

## Strategy

Telos will have 150,000 health by the start of phase 4, which is further divided into three segments of 37,500 health. Likewise, it will break free of stuns and binds every 9.6 seconds. Try to set up a rotation that can deal 37,500 damage in an instant, such as a five-stack Volley of Souls just as he launches the bomb, as damage immunity is lifted at that point. Alternatively, players could try to force spam its Freedom by binding it with ice spells.

achievements.wikiText:
We Will Fight in the Shade is an achievement that requires the player and their group to defeat Astellarn, the first boss in the Dragonkin Laboratory, without having taken more than 10,000 total damage from her solar storm.

This achievement can only be completed in normal mode and may be completed solo.

The solar storm the achievement refers to is her celestial rain that appears on the arena when she reaches 200,000 health. The rain deals around 50 damage every half-tick for players standing in the affected area, which will rapidly increase to 600 damage as it persists. When the rain changes position, the damage resets back to the minimum amount.

## Trivia

• The achievement's name is a reference to an apocryphal statement attributed to either Dienekes or Leonidas.

achievements.wikiSummary: Web Protection is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Araxxi after using the correct protection prayer against all of her basic attacks in phase 4.
achievements.wikiText:
Web Protection is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Araxxi after using the correct protection prayer against all of her basic attacks in phase 4.

This achievement can only be completed in a private instance.

## Strategy

Araxxi attacks with all three combat styles in phase 4. From a distance, Araxxi will attack with magic and ranged, while those in melee distance will be subjected to melee and magic attacks.

At a distance, Araxxi attacks with magic if no overheads protection prayers/curses are used, but will swap to ranged if she detects Protect/Deflect Magic until the player stops praying against magic. The ranged attack travels slower than the magic ones, and it is important to properly position or they may attack on the same tick.

At melee distance, Araxxi will attack indiscriminately with both melee and magic without taking prayers/curses into account. The melee attack has a faster animation than the magic one, so Protect/Deflect Melee should be the main prayer, swapping to Protect/Deflect Magic if she uses otherwise.

infobox.Description: Defeat Araxxi after using the correct protection prayer against all of her basic attacks in phase 4.

Welcome to Gielinor, it's cooler here is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Zamorak, Lord of Chaos at 750% or higher enrage while letting every chaos demon leave Infernus.

## Strategy

This achievement requires that every time Zamorak uses his 'Infernal Tomb' special attack, the chaos demon is allowed to leave infernus. When it does so, the chaos demon will gain increased stats and do more damage. The demon may be killed once it reaches the main boss arena.

Alternatively, this achievement may be completed by preventing Zamorak from using the 'Infernal Tomb' special attack entirely, by bursting Zamorak's health down to the next phase before he can use a special attack in phase 2. This assumes that Zamorak only has time to use one special attack in the other phases, for a more detailed description of how special attack skips work see the strategy guide.

achievements.name: What Do You Mean I Could Make Multiple Trips?
achievements.wikiTitle: What Do You Mean I Could Make Multiple Trips?
achievements.description: Defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 1000% or higher enrage after charging all 4 Fragments of Tumeken at once in phase 5.
achievements.wikiSummary: What Do You Mean I Could Make Multiple Trips? is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 1,000% or higher enrage after charging all 4 fragments of Tumeken at once in phase 5.
achievements.wikiText:
What Do You Mean I Could Make Multiple Trips? is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 1,000% or higher enrage after charging all 4 fragments of Tumeken at once in phase 5.

## Requirements

This achievement requires that all 4 fragments are fully charged before reforming Tumeken during phase 5 of the Amascut fight. It also requires that the enrage of the fight is at least 1000%, although completing it at 2000% is one of the requirements for the perfect achievement.

This achievement is failed if Tumeken is reformed before all 4 fragments are fully charged, which will display the message You have failed: What Do You Mean I Could Make Multiple Trips?..

## Strategy

Amascut will periodically summon Lightstealer salawa akh in phase 5 for every fragment that is at least partially charged. These spawn at the south steps and will travel toward the fragments, unless they are attacked by a player to draw their aggro. Note that if a salawa akh is hit while it is still invulnerable while on the steps, then it will not then aggro onto any player, even if using the Provoke ability.

### Safest method

To maximise the number of players able to control the akh, the team should fully charge both of the western fragments (or east, if the team prefers) before switching sides and then charging both of the remaining fragments. The distribution of players is as such:

• One player ("solo charge") forming a chain from the furthest statue on the west to the furthest fragment.
• One player ("south charge") standing by the nearer statue on the west side, forming a chain to:
• Two players ("green 1" and "green 2") who alternate between continuing the chain to the nearer fragment, and standing directly in front of Amascut to intercept her green projectiles which target the statues.
• One player ("wrangler") standing by the spawn of the feline akh, to take their aggro and kill them.

When the sides switch, the wrangler has a harder job as there are more salawa akh spawning so some may get past them, and the green 1 & 2 players will start taking 4 hits at a time, so defensive abilities are recommended. Once all 4 fragments are charged, the solo charge and south charge players may assist in killing any remaining akh, and Tumeken may be reformed when the team is ready for it. Since charging all 4 fragments at once gives less time to do damage to Amascut in phase 5, players are advised to be ready to throw out a strong DPS rotation as Amascut jumps around.

### Fastest method

A faster method is possible, meaning less time for akh to spawn. The distribution of players is as such:

• Two players ("solo west" and "solo east") each forming a chain from the furthest statue on each side to the furthest fragment on that side.
• One player ("south charge") standing by the nearer statue on the west side, forming a chain to:
• Two players ("green 1" and "green 2") who alternate between continuing the chain to the nearer fragment, and standing directly in front of Amascut to intercept her green projectiles which target the statues.

Once the south charge, green 1, and green 2 player have half-charged the near west fragment, they switch sides to fully charge the near east fragment. When the solo chargers have fully charged their fragments, they they form a chain to finish charging the half-charged near west statue. This in total saves approximately 15 seconds, which prevents around 8 additional akh from spawning. However, this method has no dedicated wrangler for the akh, so they must be taken care of by any player whom they pass, without that player leaving their position in their chain. As with the safer method, charging all 4 fragments at once gives less time to do damage to Amascut in phase 5, so players are advised to be ready to throw out a strong DPS rotation as Amascut jumps around.

Completing this achievement at 2000% enrage is one of the requirements for the Amascut, the Devourer (perfect) grandmaster achievement.

achievements.name: Working With Myself
achievements.description: Defeat Kerapac, the bound in hard mode, solo without letting any of your echoes die.
achievements.wikiSummary: Working With Myself is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Kerapac, the bound in solo hard mode encounter without letting any of your echoes die.
achievements.wikiText:
Working With Myself is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Kerapac, the bound in solo hard mode encounter without letting any of your echoes die.

## Strategy

Initiate phase 4 while having as much adrenaline as possible.

Each player clone has 10,000 life points (regardless of the player's own stats and boosts) and will fight a single echo of Kerapac which has 100,000 life points. They will not be able to hold against them for long.

Entering a player clone will copy all of their stats at the time of entry, which can be manipulated with Warp Time to quickly reset cooldowns and start with their entered stats. A powerburst of vitality is recommended as it can be used to double a clone's health. The procedure for this is:

• Enter a clone that is at or near full health. The first clone entered is often used for this, referred to as player clone A.
• Drink a powerburst of vitality, which will double player clone A's health to 20,000
• Switch to a different player clone before the powerburst effect ends, referred to as player clone B. Player clone A's health will remain at 20,000.
• Upon entering player clone B, the powerburst effect will be removed, so the player will have their health halved to 5,000. Restore health with food or potions.
• Quickly kill echo of Kerapac for clone B. Once an echo of Kerapac is defeated, the corresponding player clone disappears.
• At this point, each of player clones A and C will have taken 5,000–8,000 damage, depending on the speed at which echo of Kerapac for clone B was killed. This means that player clone A will have around 12,000 life points and player clone C will have around 2,000 life points. If the player's damage is not high enough to kill the echo of Kerapac for clone B before the other player clones take 10,000 damage and die, see below.
• Enter player clone C, which will be low on health. Restore health with food or potions.
• Quickly kill the echo of Kerapac for clone C, so that player clone C disappears.
• Enter player clone A again, which will be low on health. Restore health with food or potions.
• At this point the achievement is basically complete if the kill is successful.

If the player is unable to burst kill an echo of Kerapac before the next player clone dies, then it will be required to juggle the player clones' health. Whenever any clone is getting low on life points, enter that clone and eat some high-healing food such as sailfish or drink Saradomin brews, before returning to killing the echo of Kerapac with the lowest life points. Prioritise killing one echo of Kerapac as fast as possible to make its corresponding player clone disappear so that fewer clones need to be healed. Switching clones will interrupt any damage rotation the player is doing, and since high-healing food often drains adrenaline, this method will be slower.

## Achievement set

If this achievement is completed in a solo hard mode kill alongside Shatterproof, Ready, Set, Go!, and Definitely Can't Touch This, it will award the Kerapac, the bound (perfect) grandmaster achievement.

achievements.name: Xau-take a Leave of Absence
achievements.description: Defeat the Ambassador without anyone intercepting any of his 'Circle of Black Hands' attacks.
achievements.wikiSummary: Xau-take a Leave of Absence is an achievement that requires the player to defeat The Ambassador without anyone intercepting any of his 'Circle of Black Hands' attacks.
achievements.wikiText:
Xau-take a Leave of Absence is an achievement that requires the player to defeat The Ambassador without anyone intercepting any of his 'Circle of Black Hands' attacks.

## Strategy

When the Ambassador hits 400,000 health, the final phase of the fight starts where Seiryu the Azure Serpent will appear and kill off the Crassian ritual keepers in the arena. Shortly afterwards, the Ambassador will subdue Seiryu and summon twelve black hands, which will heal him a bit. These cannot be blocked, so players do not need to worry about needing to stay out of the way.

Afterwards, one of the twelve hands will slam the ground, indicating that it is sending energy to heal the boss. If not blocking its path, the energy will appear white. This energy heals 2,500 per cloud and each hand sends three clouds. If blocking its path, the energy will appear black and this will fail the achievement. A good strategy to always avoid the healing hand is by standing on the other side of it.

If the Ambassador is killed before the hands begin to heal him, it will also successfully complete this achievement.

## Trivia

• The name of the achievement is a play on words involving the phrase "should take a leave of absence" and the name of the entity The Ambassador tried to summon, Xau-Tak.
• A leave of absence is a formal period of time away from work or duties, usually granted for personal reasons.

achievements.wikiText:
Yakamaru (duo) is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Yakamaru in a team of 2 or fewer. When players attempt to complete this achievement in duo mode, the achievement will fail if one player dies, even if one player achieves the kill.

## Strategy

Utilise normal Yakamaru strategies in order to defeat the boss. Due to the decreased amount of damage, players will take longer to clear each phase, mandating the use of defensive abilities. Use Freedom to clear off drenched stacks whenever possible, as these stacks will deal increased damage. Using Intercept and Heal Other in combination with Barricade is useful for reducing a lot of damage, especially for the Soak attack (players turning blue) which deals 12,000 hard typeless damage across 4 hits. A beast of burden (Pack Mammoth with its scrolls) is highly recommended to store extra food. Devotion, Devoted, and Enhanced Devoted are especially useful because Yakamaru only attacks with one combat style depending on proximity, and because the drenched stacks will increase the damage of auto attacks drastically.

The DPS role will double as a poison tank, and it is the base tank's responsibility to be CPR at the end of each phase. Both players will be accumulating stacks, so try to clear them off as quick as possible. Kill off all jellyfish before starting the next phase. This also includes the ones Yakamaru summons itself, as these will deal a lot of damage. The DPS will not take damage from Yakamaru if they are in combat with something else and are not in melee range, so they can safely Soul Split until the last jellyfish is killed. If one player is attacking a jellyfish while Yakamaru uses the sand special attack, it will instead skip the sand special attack. The DPS can use this to their advantage by killing the spawned jellyfish during sand pool slowly until the sand special attack would occur. Players can go far south or far north of the arena out of Yakamaru's attack range to kill jellyfish, freedom drenched stacks, restore hitpoints, and sort their inventory.

During mirage phase, each player is responsible for handling two images of Yakamaru, as leaving one out of combat will result in it flinging projectiles to the entire team that deal 2,000 damage. The shark and stun pools should be dealt with first as fast as possible, as each player can simply carry ten planks to seal up the pool in a single action. The sand and tentacle pools are more difficult, as filling it with sand is much slower, resulting in players having to clear the pool again. If possible, when a mirage pool is killed and ready to be filled with sand, the player attacking the other pool can quickly surge to the pool to help fill it with sand, which can cut the fight down by 1 or 2 cycles of pool revivals. The players should use all defensive abilities at their disposal, as they will quickly accumulate damage stacks with two mirages attacking them at once.

achievements.name: You Shall Not Heal
achievements.description: Defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 1000% or higher enrage without allowing her to heal through 'Healing in Strength'.
achievements.wikiSummary: You Shall Not Heal is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 1,000% or higher enrage without allowing her to heal through 'Healing in Strength'.
achievements.wikiText:
You Shall Not Heal is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Amascut, the Devourer at 1,000% or higher enrage without allowing her to heal through 'Healing in Strength'.

## Requirements

'Healing in Strength' is an effect present on Amascut during Phase 4, and again in phase 7 if she targets the statue of Het. While she has this effect, Amascut will be healed whenever any of her minions damages any player.

This achievement requires that Amascut does not heal from this effect, so it requires that no player is hit by a minion in phase 4, or in phase 7 when she targets the statue of Het. The enrage of the fight must be at least 1000%.

This achievement is failed if any minion hits any player while Amascut has the buff. The message You have failed: You Shall Not Heal. is displayed if this happens.

## Strategy

### Phase 4

The minions present in phase 4 are feline guard akhs, gatekeeper gorilla akhs, and explosive scarab akhs. The gorillas and guards should be hit with Entangle or Ice Barrage to bind them so that they cannot hit players, and then killed before the bind expires. The explosive scarabs must be prevented from damaging players by only killing the scarabs required to remove the necessary shields, with any unnecessarily killed scarabs thrown out of the arena entirely before they can explode. It is not required to throw all of the scarabs out of the arena, as they constantly respawn. When the scarabs detonate at the end of phase 4, Amascut no longer has the 'Healing in Strength' buff so the hits will not fail this achievement.

### Phase 7

If Amascut targets the Crondis or Scabaras statue in phase 7, then the modest crocodile demons and explosive scarab akhs summoned by the statues should be killed before the cycle ends. If the minions are still alive when Amascut later targets the Het statue, then their hits will fail this achievement.

## Strategy

The chaos demon can only attack players in melee distance, so the use of Sticky bombs or Entangle allows the demon to be kept alive and also away from players. Care must be taken with multi-target abilities (such as Death Skulls) that the demon is far enough away to not be accidentally damaged by them.

You. Shall. Not. Shield. is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Zamorak, Lord of Chaos at 750% or higher enrage without any player in the fight using shield defensive abilities.

## Strategy

This is specific to abilities in the defence ability book that require a shield or bone shield to be able to use them. Other abilities in the defensive book such as Freedom, Anticipation, Devotion, Debilitate, and Natural Instinct can be used without invalidating the achievement.

## Achievement Set

Completing this achievement in the same kill as the following other achievements is one of the requirements for the Zamorak, Lord of Chaos (unorthodox) grandmaster achievement.

• You're coming home with me
• Stunlocked
• I said E, not E!
• Welcome to Gielinor, it's cooler here
• You. Shall. Not. Shield.
• Unpr-edict-able

achievements.name: Zamehameha
achievements.description: Defeat Zamorak, Lord of Chaos at 1,000% or higher enrage after letting him fully charge his world-ending attack in phase 7.
achievements.wikiSummary: Zamehameha is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Zamorak, Lord of Chaos at 1,000% or higher enrage after letting him fully charge his world-ending attack in phase 7.
achievements.wikiText:
Zamehameha is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Zamorak, Lord of Chaos at 1,000% or higher enrage after letting him fully charge his world-ending attack in phase 7.

## Strategy

At 1,000% enrage and above, Zamorak's charge on his world-ending attack does not reset to 0% between cycles. Therefore the most reliable way to complete this achievement is to take two cycles to complete phase 7, as the achievement does not require that Zamorak fully charge the world-ending attack on the first cycle. Zamorak has 250,000 health in phase 7 at 1,000% enrage or higher, so he should be brought low but not killed on the first cycle, ideally below around 50,000 health.

After the first cycle, the chaos demon should be killed and then the player need only wait until the red bar reaches its maximum at 100,000 damage. Since there is no time pressure limit the charge on the red bar, the player can prepare as much as they like to deal the remaining damage to Zamorak before the damage from the world-ending attack is dealt. Useful abilities that can be prepared before finishing off the last rune are:

• Applying debuffs such as Vulnerability, Smoke Cloud, and Invoke Death.
• Natural Instinct can be used to gain adrenaline quickly after spending it on an ultimate.
• A damage boosting ultimate such as Berserk, Death's Swiftness, Sunshine, or Living Death.
• Devotion alongside praying melee to avoid taking the melee hit before the world-ending attack.
• Immortality and/or equipping a Ring of death to survive for a short time after the world-ending attack hits.

There is enough time for around 4 abilities to be used after killing the last rune, in which to finish off Zamorak and win the fight.

## Trivia

• The achievement name is a reference to Goku's signature attack, "Kamehameha", in the Dragon Ball series.

achievements.wikiText:
Zamorak, Lord of Chaos (unorthodox) is an achievement that requires the player to defeat Zamorak, Lord of Chaos at 750% or higher enrage while completing the listed achievements.

These listed achievements are all part of the Combat subcategory Zamorak and are all members-only.

Completing this achievement will grant all players in the group the title [Name], the UnprEDICTable.

## Strategy

### Phases 1-6

### Special attacks

Performing a damage burst as each pad is charged can reduce or eliminate the number of Zamorak's special attacks that must be dealt with. In particular, the 'Infernal Tomb' and 'Decimate' special attacks must always be skipped, since Stunlocked requires players to take the maximum damage from these specials and You. Shall. Not. Shield. prevents players from using defensive abilities such as Immortality to survive that damage. Skipping the special attacks altogether does not invalidate the Stunlocked or Welcome to Gielinor, it's cooler here achievements. Skipping every special attack is not required to complete this achievement, although it will award Can't touch this III, and if they are not skipped then the other special attacks can be dealt with (without invalidating You. Shall. Not. Shield.) as follows:

• Flames of Zamorak: Use Devotion and melee prayer to avoid the initial 2 hits of melee damage, then use Debilitate/Disruption Shield/powerburst of vitality to survive the followup typeless hit.
• Adrenaline Cage: The base uses Devotion and magic prayer to survive, if they do not have devotion available then Intercept can be used by another player who has it available.
• Rune of Destruction: deal with as normal, no special defensive use is necessary.

The hardest phase to achieve a mechanic skip is phase 1 as the protector will spawn and reduce the damage dealt to Zamorak, which will result in a 'Flames of Zamorak' special attack if the skip is not achieved.

### Pads

The pad order is specified by Unpr-edict-able, which is 3-5-6-1-4-2. This pad order is actually rather lenient in phases 1-6 as it does not include the hexes Twinshot (pad 1) or Disintegrate (pad 4) until late in the order, which reduces the need for food or defensive abilities to mitigate damage. However the downside is that the edicts Anima Flow (pad 1) and Haste (pad 2) are also not active for much of this portion of the fight, so adrenaline gain will be normal and cooldowns will remain long.

Care should be taken with the Chaos Traps (pad 5) that appear on each pad after phase 2. These can be cleared by using either Anticipation/Freedom and Devotion, or the Sword of Edicts buff from standing near the center of the arena. It is recommended to clear the pads before the witch is killed, so that the pad will not charge prematurely, and clearing will not interfere with the preparation for the damage burst.

### Phase 7

Phase 7 is particularly difficult due to the pad order required by Unpr-edict-able, and the additional setup required to complete I said E, not E! and You're coming home with me. At 750% enrage, Zamorak has 209k health per player.

### Chaos Demon

The chaos demon must not be killed, to complete You're coming home with me. It should be lured to the back of the arena away from Zamorak and entangled, which lasts for 24 seconds. Depending on the time needed to perform the rest of the setup, it may need to be entangled multiple times.

### Incorrect rune

At least one rune must be killed out of order to complete I said E, not E!. This only has to happen once, in the case of multiple cycles. Since the player cannot use shield abilities, the damage from this rune is best dealt with by using Disruption Shield. If there are necromancers on the team, then killing the B rune allows them to use Death Skulls against Zamorak. If the B rune is the last rune, then it can be killed before the second-to-last rune to avoid accidentally starting early.

This can also be done after the correct runes are killed.

### One Cycle strategy

The best way to defeat phase 7 is to make use of a damage rotation that kills Zamorak even if his red health bar reaches 100k. This removes the need to perform all of the setup quickly to reduce the amount of damage taken, and allows players to instead perform the setup at their own pace.

• The chaos demon is kept entangled at the back of the arena.
• The incorrect rune is killed and Disruption Shield is used to survive the damage.

And then a large amount of preparation is made to deal 209k damage in a short amount of time, such as:

• Damage boosting ultimate abilities (Sunshine, Death's Swiftness or Living Death)
• Adrenaline gaining abilities (Natural Instinct, Tsunami or Imbue: Shadows)
• Damage debuffs (vulnerability bombs, Command Vengeful Ghost, Smoke Cloud or Invoke Death)
• Player buffs (Split Soul or Split Soul (special attack))
• Stacks (Wen arrow, Residual Soul, Necrosis)
• Player health below 60% to make use of Balance of Power Edict.

To survive for long enough to do the damage, Devotion and melee prayer should be used for the melee hit, and a ring of death worn to survive the 100k typeless hit. A sign of life or the effect of the Defence cape should not be used, as it takes priority over the ring of death but drains the player's adrenaline and removes many useful buffs.

### One Cycle strategy (melee)

Players using melee who have access to the Ek-ZekKil can easily subdue Zamorak in one cycle while also completing I said E, not E! achievement through the use of Greater Barge. However, this is far easier to accomplish is a solo setting due to the lowered life points of the runes.

• Make sure the Chaos Demon is entangled, so that it cannot disable your Disruption Shield.
• Meteor Strike the first rune and subdue it as normal.
• Anticipate and Surge to Zamorak
• Active Berserk then use Greater Barge on Zamorak
• Click off of Zamorak, use Devotion while praying melee. Make sure Disruption Shield is active.
• Bleed Greater Flurry on the second rune from afar. This can be accomplished by targeting the rune, activating Greater Flurry, then running back up to Zamorak.
• Greater Flurry will continue to bleed against the rune even when its subdued. It's important to have Disruption Shield active to tank the bulk of the explosion. Overkilling the rune will qualify the player for I said E, not E!.
• As the rune is being dwindled, use Chaos Roar on Zamorak.
• A simple rotation of Igneous Showdown, Overpower, Hurricane, and either The Final Flurry or Punish will be more than enough to defeat Zamorak at 750% enrage before his large hit. Make sure you have Devotion up for the initial melee slam. If the rotation is not enough, use a Powerburst of Vitality after using Hurricane.

### Two cycle strategy

Attempting to complete this achievement without one-cycling Zamorak as mentioned above is not recommended, as You. Shall. Not. Shield. prevents the use of Immortality to survive the second typeless hit. If it is needed to do so, then the strategy is:

• Kill the runes as fast as possible, to limit the amount of damage that Zamorak will do. Entangle the demon during this time.
• Use Devotion and melee prayer to survive the first melee hit.
• Use Anticipation, Debilitate, and a powerburst of vitality to survive the first typeless hit and the 4 smaller typeless hits
• Use Disruption Shield to survive the second melee hit. Be careful that the demon does not snipe it.
• Use a sign of life to survive the second typeless hit.

At this point, Zamorak's health should be low enough to comfortably finish the second cycle regardless of the size of the red bar. Take it slow, keep entangling the demon, use Disruption Shield to survive killing an incorrect rune, and burst down Zamorak when properly prepared.

Flight skipping is essentially mandatory for this achievement, and a secondary style is required in order to deal the damage dealt within the time frame.

It is still possible to clear both Zemouregal and Vorkath within the time frame, however this is even riskier due to the additional damage needed on Vorkath.
